# GitHub tracker comment

Use GitHub-flavored Markdown in `outputs/response.md` for GitHub issue
comments and descriptions. Your output is posted to the issue as-is — every
construct must render natively on GitHub.

- Headings: `##`, `###`
- Bullets: `- item`
- Numbered lists: `1. item`
- Bold: `**text**`
- Inline code: `` `code` ``
- Code block: ` ```lang ... ``` ` with a language tag (`dart`, `bash`, `json`)
- Link: `[text](url)`
- Tables: standard GFM table syntax (`|---|` separator row)

Do not use Jira wiki markup in GitHub fields: no `{code}...{code}` blocks,
no `{panel}` macros, no `h1.`/`h2.`/`h3.` heading prefixes, no
`{{monospace}}` inline code, no `[title|url]` links. None of it renders on
GitHub — a comment full of `{code}` fences and `h3.` headers is unreadable.

**IMPORTANT** When the issue references a parent story or related issues,
get them for full context using: `dmtools github_get_issue OWNER/REPO#NUMBER`
(the composite key form works directly).

# gh-1044: [BUG] iOS/MACos: AIIN (aiin.by) provider add — auth flow completes but provider never added; reconfigure binds to the CodeMie row

## Description

## Bug

On **iOS**, adding the **aiin.by** provider: the auth flow runs (loopback callback listener starts, browser sheet opens, sign-in completes on the page) — but **the AIIN provider never appears** in the providers list. Owner report (2026-09-28): «пытаюсь добавить aiin.by провайдер... прохожу auth flow но провайдер не добавляется. на ios». Owner rulings: AIIN «работает охрененно в браузере» (web reference behavior), and it must work exactly as well **on mobile and macOS** (app builds). Third ruling (2026-09-28, verbatim): «никаких фолбек на ключ... у нас там честный SSO должен быть... если что-то не получится то тогда надо будет мне в aiin.by адопшен запрашивать» — **no key-paste fallback at all; SSO is the only path**; if the SSO cannot be made to work client-side, the deliverable is a precise, evidence-backed adoption request for aiin.by (what to change on their side).

## Evidence (app log, iOS device, 2026-09-28)

```
11:33:03 [AIIN mobile] listening for the AIIN callback on http://127.0.0.1:65043/callback
11:33:32 [AIIN mobile] listening for the AIIN callback on http://127.0.0.1:65049/callback
11:33:35 [AIIN mobile] browser opened; sign in on the AIIN page
11:33:53 [Fa] reconfigure: baseUrl=https://codemie.lab.epam.com/code-assistant-api/v1,
           apiKey.len=190, isCodeMie=true, model.headers=[cookie]
11:33:58 [AIIN mobile] listening for the AIIN callback on http://127.0.0.1:65057/callback
```

Three listener starts (three Add taps), the browser sheet opened — and then **zero AIIN completion artifacts**: no model-picker push, no `[Fa] reconfigure` with `api.aiin.by`, no registry entry. The 11:33:53 reconfigure is **codemie** — see F4 below; it is NOT the AIIN flow (`_finishAiinConnect` always reconfigures with `aiinDefaultChatBaseUrl`).

## What the code does (read on origin/main; the local checkout predates this flow)

`flutter_app/lib/services/aiin_connect_flow.dart`:
- `runAiinConnectFlow` dispatches: web → `runAiinWebConnect` (the working popup path, #486); **mobile (iOS/Android) → `runAiinMobileConnect`** (#976); desktop → `_runAiinDesktopConnect`.
- `runAiinMobileConnect` runs the SAME loopback CLI server as desktop (`runAiinConnectCliFlow`, `lib/src/cli/aiin_connect_server.dart:152` logs the "listening" line) and opens the authorize URL in an **ASWebAuthenticationSession** sheet via the shared `fah/web_auth_session` MethodChannel (line ~311 — the same channel the CodeMie SSO flow drives).
- The design: the OAuth redirect (`http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback`) loads **inside the sheet**, hits the on-device server, `onCallback` dismisses the sheet, the server exchanges the code and returns `AiinConnectResult`.
- **`cancelWhenOpenSettles: authSession`** (iOS): the sheet resolving WITHOUT a server callback is treated as user cancel → `_completeAiinConnect` gets `result == null` → **silent paste-key fallback** (`_pasteAiinKeyFallback`). A user swipe and a lost race are indistinguishable by design.
- Success path: `_finishAiinConnect` → model picker from `api.aiin.by/v1/models` → registry entry named by account email → `service.reconfigure` (logs `baseUrl=api.aiin.by`).

## The CodeMie comparison (owner's pointer — decisive)

CodeMie SSO works on this exact iOS app through the SAME `fah/web_auth_session` channel. `AppDelegate.swift` (~lines 2284–2345) implements the native contract: `authenticate {url, callbackScheme}` creates the `ASWebAuthenticationSession`, **intercepts the redirect whose scheme matches `callbackScheme`** (iOS's RFC-8252 loopback interception), and **returns the callback URL to Dart**: `result(callbackURL?.absoluteString)` (or nil on user cancel).

CodeMie's Dart (`codemie_sso_flow.dart`, `systemAuthSessionCodeMieSso`) invokes it with **`callbackScheme: "http"`**, the redirect is `http://localhost:<port>/?token=...`, and the flow **consumes the returned URL** — extracting the token right out of it. WebView fallback only when the session cannot start.

AIIN's `_openAiinAuthSession` (aiin_connect_flow.dart ~319) breaks the contract in exactly two places:
1. **No `callbackScheme`** — it sends only `{'url': url}`; native reads `args["callbackScheme"]` → nil → **no interception**: the `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback` redirect becomes a plain in-sheet navigation, and the session's completion handler fires only on cancel.
2. **The return value is discarded** — `.then((_) => true)` throws the intercepted URL (when there is one) on the floor. CodeMie's flow builds its credentials from that URL; AIIN's Dart never looks at it.

So the flow's completion hinges entirely on the in-sheet navigation physically reaching the dart:io loopback server — the flakiest possible leg — while the proven mechanism (scheme interception + returned URL) sits one argument away. Owner's intuition confirmed: «и aiin.by тоже должна быть возможность легко получать это».

The AIIN provider definition is correct — `lib/src/providers/aiin_auth.dart:31-34` (`auth.aiin.by` / `api.aiin.by`); the endpoint hypothesis is **disproven** by code. The failure is in the mobile surface plumbing.

## Failure modes to discriminate (instrument first)

- **F2 — CONFIRMED wiring defect (primary)**: no `callbackScheme` in the `authenticate` call + the returned callback URL discarded (see the CodeMie comparison). With a nil scheme there is no interception; completion hinges on the in-sheet navigation reaching the dart:io server, and the race/cancel semantics (`cancelWhenOpenSettles`) then eat the flow. Fix is client-side: wire AIIN's session exactly like CodeMie's.
- **F1 — proxy blocks the redirect (remaining question)**: if the AIIN OAuth proxy refuses the `http://127.0.0.1` redirect target server-side (old code comment: «the AIIN proxy currently blocks cross-device redirects»), no redirect fires at all — sign-in completes, nothing comes back, which is also consistent with the owner log. After the F2 fix this is cleanly detectable as «no interception AND no navigation»; it is then the case for the AC8 aiin.by adoption request.
- **F3 — listener leak**: repeated taps stack loopback servers (three live listeners across one session, ports 65043/65049/65057) — the retry path starts a new flow without tearing down the previous one.
- **F4 — connection guard hijack (side observation)**: the 11:33:53 `reconfigure` to codemie is the boot/connection guard (`agent_service_connection_guard.dart`) restoring the last-saved connection when the app returned from the auth sheet — it mutates the active connection **in the middle of the AIIN add flow**. Not the root cause of the missing provider, but an I1-class violation that compounds the confusion.

## Fix contract (owner rulings: honest SSO, no paste fallback)

1. **iOS AIIN drives `fah/web_auth_session` with the CodeMie contract**: pass `callbackScheme: 'http'`, use the `localhost` redirect host (CodeMie's proven shape, replacing `127.0.0.1`), and **consume the callback URL the channel returns** — extract `code`/`state` and feed the flow's existing code-exchange. Completion must not depend on the in-sheet navigation reaching the dart:io server.
2. The dart:io loopback server stays the desktop/macOS mechanism (CLI parity) — untouched by the iOS fix.
3. If the AC2 instrumentation then shows the proxy never issues the redirect (F1), ship the AC8 aiin.by adoption spec; until anything works the flow fails visibly (I4).
4. F3: one loopback listener per attempt — Dart-side single flight.
5. F4: the connection guard never reconfigures the active connection while an add-provider flow is in progress.

## Invariants

- **I1** — An auth flow mutates exactly the provider row it started from; the connection guard never reconfigures the active connection while an add-provider flow is in progress (F4).
- **I2** — Single flight: one loopback listener per provider-add attempt; retries tear down the previous server (F3).
- **I3** — The shared `fah/web_auth_session` channel serves AIIN and CodeMie without cross-talk (both flows drive it; a CodeMie restore must not surface mid-AIIN).

CodeMie SSO works on this exact iOS app through the SAME `fah/web_auth_session` channel. `AppDelegate.swift` (~lines 2284–2345) implements the native contract: `authenticate {url, callbackScheme}` creates the `ASWebAuthenticationSession`, **intercepts the redirect whose scheme matches `callbackScheme`** (iOS's RFC-8252 loopback interception), and **returns the callback URL to Dart**: `result(callbackURL?.absoluteString)` (or nil on user cancel).

CodeMie's Dart (`codemie_sso_flow.dart`, `systemAuthSessionCodeMieSso`) invokes it with **`callbackScheme: "http"`**, the redirect is `http://localhost:<port>/?token=...`, and the flow **consumes the returned URL** — extracting the token right out of it. WebView fallback only when the session cannot start.

AIIN's `_openAiinAuthSession` (aiin_connect_flow.dart ~319) breaks the contract in exactly two places:
1. **No `callbackScheme`** — it sends only `{'url': url}`; native reads `args["callbackScheme"]` → nil → **no interception**: the `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback` redirect becomes a plain in-sheet navigation, and the session's completion handler fires only on cancel.
2. **The return value is discarded** — `.then((_) => true)` throws the intercepted URL (when there is one) on the floor. CodeMie's flow builds its credentials from that URL; AIIN's Dart never looks at it.

So the flow's completion hinges entirely on the in-sheet navigation physically reaching the dart:io loopback server — the flakiest possible leg — while the proven mechanism (scheme interception + returned URL) sits one argument away. Owner's intuition confirmed: «и aiin.by тоже должна быть возможность легко получать это».

The AIIN provider definition is correct — `lib/src/providers/aiin_auth.dart:31-34` (`auth.aiin.by` / `api.aiin.by`); the endpoint hypothesis is **disproven** by code. The failure is in the mobile surface plumbing.

## Failure modes to discriminate (instrument first)

- **F2 — CONFIRMED wiring defect (primary)**: no `callbackScheme` in the `authenticate` call + the returned callback URL discarded (see the CodeMie comparison). With a nil scheme there is no interception; completion hinges on the in-sheet navigation reaching the dart:io server, and the race/cancel semantics (`cancelWhenOpenSettles`) then eat the flow. Fix is client-side: wire AIIN's session exactly like CodeMie's.
- **F1 — proxy blocks the redirect (remaining question)**: if the AIIN OAuth proxy refuses the `http://127.0.0.1` redirect target server-side (old code comment: «the AIIN proxy currently blocks cross-device redirects»), no redirect fires at all — sign-in completes, nothing comes back, which is also consistent with the owner log. After the F2 fix this is cleanly detectable as «no interception AND no navigation»; it is then the case for the AC8 aiin.by adoption request.
- **F3 — listener leak**: repeated taps stack loopback servers (three live listeners across one session, ports 65043/65049/65057) — the retry path starts a new flow without tearing down the previous one.
- **F4 — connection guard hijack (side observation)**: the 11:33:53 `reconfigure` to codemie is the boot/connection guard (`agent_service_connection_guard.dart`) restoring the last-saved connection when the app returned from the auth sheet — it mutates the active connection **in the middle of the AIIN add flow**. Not the root cause of the missing provider, but an I1-class violation that compounds the confusion.

## Fix contract (owner rulings: honest SSO, no paste fallback)

1. **iOS AIIN drives `fah/web_auth_session` with the CodeMie contract**: pass `callbackScheme: 'http'`, use the `localhost` redirect host (CodeMie's proven shape, replacing `127.0.0.1`), and **consume the callback URL the channel returns** — extract `code`/`state` and feed the flow's existing code-exchange. Completion must not depend on the in-sheet navigation reaching the dart:io server.
2. The dart:io loopback server stays the desktop/macOS mechanism (CLI parity) — untouched by the iOS fix.
3. If the AC2 instrumentation then shows the proxy never issues the redirect (F1), ship the AC8 aiin.by adoption spec; until anything works the flow fails visibly (I4).
4. F3: one loopback listener per attempt — Dart-side single flight.
5. F4: the connection guard never reconfigures the active connection while an add-provider flow is in progress.

## Invariants

- **I1** — An auth flow mutates exactly the provider row it started from; the connection guard never reconfigures the active connection while an add-provider flow is in progress (F4).
- **I2** — Single flight: one loopback listener per provider-add attempt; retries tear down the previous server (F3).
- **I3** — The shared `fah/web_auth_session` channel …

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/Step groups +
  collapsible turn/assistant-run summaries), `deriveTrajectoryTimeline`
  (four modes — `sequence` equal-width slots, `duration` with idle gaps
  compressed out, `time` zero-width wall-clock markers, `actual` real gaps;
  three fixed lanes: 0 system/user/context, 1 message/compacted, 2 tools),
  `trajectoryTimelineFocusIndexes` (selection → visible ledger indexes),
  and `ThrottledTrajectorySearchIndex` (full-text; matches are stable
  record ids). `formatters.dart` holds the shared duration/token/throughput
  formatting; `trajectory_preview.dart` the bounded single-line previews;
  `trajectory_export.dart` the whole-snapshot JSON/Markdown exporters the
  header's copy menu uses. Tool records carry `startedAt` (real launch
  time, distinct from the projected position) so the Gantt/actual
  projections plot true spans. Outbound model requests persist for the
  ledger as hidden `model_request_summary` `CustomRecord`s — the CLI
  event handler (`agent_event_handler.dart`, emitted through
  `agent_cli.dart`) and the app's `AgentService` both buffer a
  `TrajectoryRequestDetail` per call and flush it onto the session
  record chain right before the assistant message, so replays see it
  ahead of the reply — and `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder` folds them into
  the message record's request detail (the Request tab).
  Consumers render, never re-derive: `packages/fa_ui`'s
  `lib/src/trajectory/` widgets and the CLI `/trajectory` family.
- `lib/src/cli/trajectory_commands.dart` (a `part of` `agent_cli.dart`) +
  `lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart` — the read-only REPL family
  `/trajectory [view|cost|tail|inspect <n>]` (bare = `view`, capped at 200
  rows; `tail` follows the live session every 500ms) and the headless
  `fa trajectory <view|tail|cost|inspect> [sessionId] [--json] [--at N]`
  subcommand (`--at N` replays the snapshot as it stood at record N, view
  only). Session resolution: exact id > session-name match > most recent.
  Rendering is pure Dart in `trajectory_tui.dart` (no `dart:io`), shared by
  both entries; `bin/fah.dart` routes …

Sequence when the channel future resolves (test completes `session` synchronously inside the handler — so `invokeMethod`'s future completes... when?):

The mock handler returns `session!.future` — already completed. `invokeMethod` → `send` → handler → the messenger completes the invokeMethod future. In the REAL zone (runAsync), this happens in real microtasks.

Chain in `_openAiinAuthSession`:
```dart
return _webAuthSessionChannel
    .invokeMethod<String>('authenticate', {...})
    .then((callbackUrl) {
      debugPrint('[AIIN mobile] sign-in sheet resolved; callbackUrl=...');
      return callbackUrl;
    });
```
- invokeMethod future completes with the URL → `.then` listener scheduled → runs: logs "sheet resolved", returns → the returned (then-chained) future completes with URL.

In the wrapper:
```dart
final callbackUrl = await _openAiinAuthSession(url);
```
- await on that chained future → schedules wrapper resumption.
- wrapper resumes: intercepted.complete(url); return true → openBrowserFn's Future completes → schedules _openAiinBrowser's `await openBrowserFn(...)` resumption.

So hops:
H1: then-callback logs "sheet resolved" → chained future completes → schedules H2.
H2: wrapper resumes → intercepted.complete(url) [schedules H3 = intercepted.then listener] → return true [schedules H4 = _openAiinBrowser resumption].

H4: _openAiinBrowser resumes: onStatus('browser opened...') → openBrowserFn returned true → _openAiinBrowser returns → `opened` completes [schedules H6 = opened.then listener].
H5: Future.any resolves with the pair → runAiinConnectCliFlow resumes: `final (won, source) = await ...` → onStatus('AIIN redirect intercepted by the sign-in sheet...').
H6: opened.then: cancelWhenOpenSettles=true, surfaceClosed not completed, interceptedCallback IS completed → guard false → nothing.

1. "sheet resolved; callbackUrl=returned"
2. "browser opened; sign in on the AIIN page"

OBSERVED order:

2. "browser opened; sign in on the AIIN page"
3. "the sign-in sheet closed without completing the sign-in (no callback returned — user cancel)"

```dart
static Future _returnAsyncNotFuture(Object suspendState, Object? returnValue) {
  _Future future = ...;

An async function returning a non-Future value completes its future **SYNCHRONOUSLY** at the `return` statement (`_completeWithValue` — inline propagation of ALL listeners: `.then` callbacks AND await resumptions run RIGHT THERE).

Whereas `Completer.complete()` (an `_AsyncCompleter`) goes through `_asyncComplete` → `_asyncCompleteWithValue` → **`scheduleMicrotask`** — the listeners run in a LATER microtask!

Hence the observed order: L2, done, ..., L1. The async-fn return JUMPS THE QUEUE ahead of any completer completed earlier in the same stretch.

In the mobile openBrowserFn wrapper:
```dart

  if (intercepted != null && !intercepted.isCompleted) {

```

So at `return true`:

1. `intercepted.complete(url)` schedules its `.then` listener as a MICROTASK (async completer).
2. The wrapper's `return true` SYNCHRONOUSLY cascades: wrapper future → _openAiinBrowser await resumption → onStatus → _openAiinBrowser's own return → `opened`'s completion (synchronous) → the `cancelWhenOpenSettles` guard runs IMMEDIATELY, BEFORE the queued intercepted listener ever gets a chance.

The `intercepted` FUTURE being pending ≠ no callback coming. The real semantics: `cancelWhenOpenSettles` exists for the sheet that closed WITHOUT delivering a callback. comments and descriptions. Your output is posted to the issue as-is — every

- Code block: ` ```lang ... ``` ` with a language tag (`dart`, `bash`, `json`)

no `{panel}` macros, no `h1.`/`h2.`/`h3.` heading prefixes, no
`{{monospace}}` inline code, no `[title|url]` links. None of it renders on
GitHub — a comment full of `{code}` fences and `h3.` headers is unreadable.

# gh-1044: [BUG] iOS/MACos: AIIN (aiin.by) provider add — auth flow completes but provider never added; reconfigure binds to the CodeMie row

## Description

## Bug

On **iOS**, adding the **aiin.by** provider: the auth flow runs (loopback callback listener starts, browser sheet opens, sign-in completes on the page) — but **the AIIN provider never appears** in the providers list. Owner report (2026-09-28): «пытаюсь добавить aiin.by провайдер... прохожу auth flow но провайдер не добавляется. на ios». Owner rulings: AIIN «работает охрененно в браузере» (web reference behavior), and it must work exactly as well **on mobile and macOS** (app builds). Third ruling (2026-09-28, verbatim): «никаких фолбек на ключ... у нас там честный SSO должен быть... если что-то не получится то тогда надо будет мне в aiin.by адопшен запрашивать» — **no key-paste fallback at all; SSO is the only path**; if the SSO cannot be made to work client-side, the deliverable is a precise, evidence-backed adoption request for aiin.by (what to change on their side).

## Evidence (app log, iOS device, 2026-09-28)

```
11:33:03 [AIIN mobile] listening for the AIIN callback on http://127.0.0.1:65043/callback
11:33:32 [AIIN mobile] listening for the AIIN callback on http://127.0.0.1:65049/callback
11:33:35 [AIIN mobile] browser opened; sign in on the AIIN page
11:33:53 [Fa] reconfigure: baseUrl=https://codemie.lab.epam.com/code-assistant-api/v1,
           apiKey.len=190, isCodeMie=true, model.headers=[cookie]
11:33:58 [AIIN mobile] listening for the AIIN callback on http://127.0.0.1:65057/callback
```

Three listener starts (three Add taps), the browser sheet opened — and then **zero AIIN completion artifacts**: no model-picker push, no `[Fa] reconfigure` with `api.aiin.by`, no registry entry. The 11:33:53 reconfigure is **codemie** — see F4 below; it is NOT the AIIN flow (`_finishAiinConnect` always reconfigures with `aiinDefaultChatBaseUrl`).

## What the code does (read on origin/main; the local checkout predates this flow)

`flutter_app/lib/services/aiin_connect_flow.dart`:
- `runAiinConnectFlow` dispatches: web → `runAiinWebConnect` (the working popup path, #486); **mobile (iOS/Android) → `runAiinMobileConnect`** (#976); desktop → `_runAiinDesktopConnect`.
- `runAiinMobileConnect` runs the SAME loopback CLI server as desktop (`runAiinConnectCliFlow`, `lib/src/cli/aiin_connect_server.dart:152` logs the "listening" line) and opens the authorize URL in an **ASWebAuthenticationSession** sheet via the shared `fah/web_auth_session` MethodChannel (line ~311 — the same channel the CodeMie SSO flow drives).
- The design: the OAuth redirect (`http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback`) loads **inside the sheet**, hits the on-device server, `onCallback` dismisses the sheet, the server exchanges the code and returns `AiinConnectResult`.
- **`cancelWhenOpenSettles: authSession`** (iOS): the sheet resolving WITHOUT a server callback is treated as user cancel → `_completeAiinConnect` gets `result == null` → **silent paste-key fallback** (`_pasteAiinKeyFallback`). A user swipe and a lost race are indistinguishable by design.
- Success path: `_finishAiinConnect` → model picker from `api.aiin.by/v1/models` → registry entry named by account email → `service.reconfigure` (logs `baseUrl=api.aiin.by`).

## The CodeMie comparison (owner's pointer — decisive)

CodeMie SSO works on this exact iOS app through the SAME `fah/web_auth_session` channel. `AppDelegate.swift` (~lines 2284–2345) implements the native contract: `authenticate {url, callbackScheme}` creates the `ASWebAuthenticationSession`, **intercepts the redirect whose scheme matches `callbackScheme`** (iOS's RFC-8252 loopback interception), and **returns the callback URL to Dart**: `result(callbackURL?.absoluteString)` (or nil on user cancel).

CodeMie's Dart (`codemie_sso_flow.dart`, `systemAuthSessionCodeMieSso`) invokes it with **`callbackScheme: "http"`**, the redirect is `http://localhost:<port>/?token=...`, and the flow **consumes the returned URL** — extracting the token right out of it. WebView fallback only when the session cannot start.

AIIN's `_openAiinAuthSession` (aiin_connect_flow.dart ~319) breaks the contract in exactly two places:
1. **No `callbackScheme`** — it sends only `{'url': url}`; native reads `args["callbackScheme"]` → nil → **no interception**: the `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback` redirect becomes a plain in-sheet navigation, and the session's completion handler fires only on cancel.
2. **The return value is discarded** — `.then((_) => true)` throws the intercepted URL (when there is one) on the floor. CodeMie's flow builds its credentials from that URL; AIIN's Dart never looks at it.

So the flow's completion hinges entirely on the in-sheet navigation physically reaching the dart:io loopback server — the flakiest possible leg — while the proven mechanism (scheme interception + returned URL) sits one argument away. Owner's intuition confirmed: «и aiin.by тоже должна быть возможность легко получать это».

The AIIN provider definition is correct — `lib/src/providers/aiin_auth.dart:31-34` (`auth.aiin.by` / `api.aiin.by`); the endpoint hypothesis is **disproven** by code. The failure is in the mobile surface plumbing.

## Failure modes to discriminate (instrument first)

- **F2 — CONFIRMED wiring defect (primary)**: no `callbackScheme` in the `authenticate` call + the returned callback URL discarded (see the CodeMie comparison). With a nil scheme there is no interception; completion hinges on the in-sheet navigation reaching the dart:io server, and the race/cancel semantics (`cancelWhenOpenSettles`) then eat the flow. Fix is client-side: wire AIIN's session exactly like CodeMie's.
- **F1 — proxy blocks the redirect (remaining question)**: if the AIIN OAuth proxy refuses the `http://127.0.0.1` redirect target server-side (old code comment: «the AIIN proxy currently blocks cross-device redirects»), no redirect fires at all — sign-in completes, nothing comes back, which is also consistent with the owner log. After the F2 fix this is cleanly detectable as «no interception AND no navigation»; it is then the case for the AC8 aiin.by adoption request.
- **F3 — listener leak**: repeated taps stack loopback servers (three live listeners across one session, ports 65043/65049/65057) — the retry path starts a new flow without tearing down the previous one.
- **F4 — connection guard hijack (side observation)**: the 11:33:53 `reconfigure` to codemie is the boot/connection guard (`agent_service_connection_guard.dart`) restoring the last-saved connection when the app returned from the auth sheet — it mutates the active connection **in the middle of the AIIN add flow**. Not the root cause of the missing provider, but an I1-class violation that compounds the confusion.

## Fix contract (owner rulings: honest SSO, no paste fallback)

1. **iOS AIIN drives `fah/web_auth_session` with the CodeMie contract**: pass `callbackScheme: 'http'`, use the `localhost` redirect host (CodeMie's proven shape, replacing `127.0.0.1`), and **consume the callback URL the channel returns** — extract `code`/`state` and feed the flow's existing code-exchange. Completion must not depend on the in-sheet navigation reaching the dart:io server.
2. The dart:io loopback server stays the desktop/macOS mechanism (CLI parity) — untouched by the iOS fix.
3. If the AC2 instrumentation then shows the proxy never issues the redirect (F1), ship the AC8 aiin.by adoption spec; until anything works the flow fails visibly (I4).
4. F3: one loopback listener per attempt — Dart-side single flight.
5. F4: the connection guard never reconfigures the active connection while an add-provider flow is in progress.

## Invariants

- **I1** — An auth flow mutates exactly the provider row it started from; the connection guard never reconfigures the active connection while an add-provider flow is in progress (F4).
- **I2** — Single flight: one loopback listener per provider-add attempt; retries tear down the previous server (F3).
- **I3** — The shared `fah/web_auth_session` channel serves AIIN and CodeMie without cross-talk (both flows drive it; a CodeMie restore must not surface mid-AIIN).

factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/Step groups +
  collapsible turn/assistant-run summaries), `deriveTrajectoryTimeline`
  (four modes — `sequence` equal-width slots, `duration` with idle gaps
  compressed out, `time` zero-width wall-clock markers, `actual` real gaps;
  three fixed lanes: 0 system/user/context, 1 message/compacted, 2 tools),
  `trajectoryTimelineFocusIndexes` (selection → visible ledger indexes),
  and `ThrottledTrajectorySearchIndex` (full-text; matches are stable
  record ids). `formatters.dart` holds the shared duration/token/throughput
  formatting; `trajectory_preview.dart` the bounded single-line previews;
  `trajectory_export.dart` the whole-snapshot JSON/Markdown exporters the
  header's copy menu uses. Tool records carry `startedAt` (real launch
  time, distinct from the projected position) so the Gantt/actual
  projections plot true spans. Outbound model requests persist for the
  ledger as hidden `model_request_summary` `CustomRecord`s — the CLI
  event handler (`agent_event_handler.dart`, emitted through
  `agent_cli.dart`) and the app's `AgentService` both buffer a
  `TrajectoryRequestDetail` per call and flush it onto the session
  record chain right before the assistant message, so replays see it
  ahead of the reply — and `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder` folds them into
  the message record's request detail (the Request tab).
  Consumers render, never re-derive: `packages/fa_ui`'s
  `lib/src/trajectory/` widgets and the CLI `/trajectory` family.
- `lib/src/cli/trajectory_commands.dart` (a `part of` `agent_cli.dart`) +
  `lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart` — the read-only REPL family
  `/trajectory [view|cost|tail|inspect <n>]` (bare = `view`, capped at 200
  rows; `tail` follows the live session every 500ms) and the headless
  `fa trajectory <view|tail|cost|inspect> [sessionId] [--json] [--at N]`
  subcommand (`--at N` replays the snapshot as it stood at record N, view
  only). Session resolution: exact id > session-name match > most recent.
  Rendering is pure Dart in `trajectory_tui.dart` (no `dart:io`), shared by
  both entries; `bin/fah.dart` routes …

`interceptedCallback?.call()` is called synchronously — for the mobile flow, `() => intercepted.future` — attach happens immediately after the openBrowserFn call started but openBrowserFn is async: `(url) async { final callbackUrl = await _openAiinAuthSession(url); ... intercepted.complete(callbackUrl); }`. **FOUND IT — SMOKING GUN:**

```dart
static Future _returnAsyncNotFuture(Object suspendState, Object? returnValue) {
  _Future future = ...;
  future._completeWithValue(returnValue);   // ← SYNCHRONOUS COMPLETION!
  return future;
}
```

An async function returning a non-Future value completes its future **SYNCHRONOUSLY** at the `return` statement (`_completeWithValue` — inline propagation of ALL listeners: `.then` callbacks AND await resumptions run RIGHT THERE).

Whereas `Completer.complete()` (an `_AsyncCompleter`) goes through `_asyncComplete` → `_asyncCompleteWithValue` → **`scheduleMicrotask`** — the listeners run in a LATER microtask!

So in `body`'s sync stretch:
1. `c.complete('x')` → schedules M_A (L1 runs in M_A, LATER).
2. `return` → `_completeWithValue` INLINE → `opened`'s listeners (L2, main's await) run RIGHT NOW.

Hence the observed order: L2, done, ..., L1. The async-fn return JUMPS THE QUEUE ahead of any completer completed earlier in the same stretch.

THIS EXPLAINS THE FLOW BUG PERFECTLY:

In the mobile openBrowserFn wrapper:
```dart
(url) async {
  final callbackUrl = await _openAiinAuthSession(url);   // sheet resolves
  if (intercepted != null && !intercepted.isCompleted) {
    intercepted.complete(callbackUrl);   // → schedules intercepted.then as MICROTASK M_A
  }
  return true;                            // → SYNCHRONOUS propagation!
}
```

`return true` synchronously completes the wrapper's future → `_openAiinBrowser`'s `await openBrowserFn(...)` resumption — wait, is the await resumption synchronous too?? `await future` where future is ALREADY complete → `_awaitCompletedFuture` → `future._zone.scheduleMicrotask(run)` — SCHEDULED. Hmm — but the await was attached when the future was INCOMPLETE → `_thenAwait` → a listener on the wrapper's future → `_completeWithValue` propagates listeners inline → the listener is the _SuspendState thenCallback wrapper → `zone.runUnary(_thenCallback, value)` — hmm, `_thenAwait` registers `_thenCallback` directly as a listener — `_completeWithValue` → `_propagateToListeners` → handleValueCallback → `listener.handleValue(sourceResult)` → calls `_thenCallback(value)` = `suspendState._resume(value, ...)` — **the await resumption runs INLINE, synchronously!**

So at `return true`:
- INLINE: _openAiinBrowser resumes: `onStatus('browser opened...')` → `_openAiinBrowser` returns → its own future completes via `_returnAsyncNotFuture` → **INLINE again**: `opened`'s listeners:
  - the guard `opened.then(...)` in `_firstCallbackOrOpenError` → runs INLINE: `cancelWhenOpenSettles=true`, `surfaceClosed` not completed, **`interceptedCallback` NOT completed** (M_A hasn't run yet — it's just queued!) → **`surfaceClosed.completeError(AiinSurfaceClosedException())`** ← THE BUG!
  - Future.any's subscription on `opened`... wait — Future.any subscribes to openError/surfaceClosed/interceptedCallback/callbackFuture — NOT to `opened` directly. The guard is the only `opened.then`.
- Then the event loop drains M_A: intercepted.then fires → url != null → interceptedCallback.complete — TOO LATE, the race already resolved with the surfaceClosed error.

CONFIRMED ROOT CAUSE — the race in `_firstCallbackOrOpenError` loses because:
1. `intercepted.complete(url)` schedules its `.then` listener as a MICROTASK (async completer).
2. The wrapper's `return true` SYNCHRONOUSLY cascades: wrapper future → _openAiinBrowser await resumption → onStatus → _openAiinBrowser's own return → `opened`'s completion (synchronous) → the `cancelWhenOpenSettles` guard runs IMMEDIATELY, BEFORE the queued intercepted listener ever gets a chance.
3. The guard's `interceptedCallback.isCompleted` check is FALSE → surfaceClosed wins → the flow cancels despite the intercepted URL being in hand.

The design comment "Completing it BEFORE the open future's bool keeps the flow's race order" was based on the WRONG microtask model — async-fn returns complete SYNCHRONOUSLY (this changed in Dart ~2.17+ when `_returnAsyncNotFuture` switched from `_asyncCompleteWithValue` to `_completeWithValue` for perf).

Options:

**Option A (flow-side)**: In the wrapper, don't `return true` synchronously after `intercepted.complete(...)` — yield first: `await Future<void>.delayed(Duration.zero)` (or `scheduleMicrotask`) AFTER intercepted.complete, THEN return true. The race then delivers via M_B (interceptedCallback listener). CORRECT.

But fragile — relies on subtle scheduling again. 

**Option B (server-side, root cause)**: the RACE itself should not treat "open settled" as cancel when an intercepted callback is still pending. The `intercepted` FUTURE being pending ≠ no callback coming. The real semantics: `cancelWhenOpenSettles` exists for the sheet that closed WITHOUT delivering a callback. But in the new AC9 contract, the SAME `authenticate` call delivers BOTH the open-settle AND the callback URL through `intercepted`. When `intercepted != null`, the "open settled without callback" signal is EXACTLY the intercepted future resolving with NULL — the `opened` settle is redundant for the auth-session surface!

Look at the wiring: for authSession, openBrowserFn completes when the SHEET RESOLVES (the await on _openAiinAuthSession), and intercepted completes from the same resolution. The `opened` completion carries NO extra information — the intercepted future is the sheet's completion value. So under the AC9 contract, `cancelWhenOpenSettles` + `opened`-settle-guard is a DUPLICATE cancel path racing (and losing) against the intercepted delivery.

Cleanest root fix in `runAiinConnectCliFlow` / `_firstCallbackOrOpenError`: when an `intercepted` future exists, the `opened` settle must NOT trigger the cancel — the intercepted future's own null resolution is the cancel signal. `cancelWhenOpenSettles` then only applies when `intercepted == null` (an external-browser surface... but wait — cancelWhenOpenSettles was introduced exactly FOR the auth-session; desktop leaves it false).

Hmm, but careful: `opened` for the auth-session wrapper resolves when the sheet settles. The intercepted future ALSO resolves then. With Option B, the guard on `opened` would be skipped entirely when intercepted != null — the cancel comes solely from intercepted == null. Same semantics, no race, and the redundant path is gone. That's the root-cause-level fix: **the race must not multiply signals that arrive from the same source with different delivery timing.**

BUT — one more consideration: what if the native side NEVER completes the intercepted future (e.g., a MissingPluginException path... no — that errors through intercepted.onError → openError ✓). If the wrapper's openBrowserFn throws BEFORE completing intercepted (e.g. _openAiinAuthSession throws PlatformException) → intercepted never completes → with the guard skipped, the cancel-on-open-settle wouldn't fire — but the open ERROR path handles it: openBrowserFn's error → await openBrowserFn throws in _openAiinBrowser → `opened` completes with error → openError → race delivers the error ✓ (the existing `onError` on the opened listener). Good.

What if openBrowserFn returns false (couldn't open)? Then `opened` completes normally (value false → hmm — `_openAiinBrowser`'s else branch: onStatus('could not open browser...')) — `opened` completes without error. With the guard skipped (intercepted != null), the flow would wait for the intercepted future... whic…

1. `intercepted.complete(url)` — queues its listener as a microtask

The `opened`-settle cancel path duplicates the intercepted future's own cancel signal (both come from the same sheet resolution) and always beats it due to this scheduling asymmetry. Use GitHub-flavored Markdown in `outputs/response.md` for GitHub issue
comments and descriptions. Your output is posted to the issue as-is — every

no `{panel}` macros, no `h1.`/`h2.`/`h3.` heading prefixes, no
`{{monospace}}` inline code, no `[title|url]` links. None of it renders on
GitHub — a comment full of `{code}` fences and `h3.` headers is unreadable.

# gh-1044: [BUG] iOS/MACos: AIIN (aiin.by) provider add — auth flow completes but provider never added; reconfigure binds to the CodeMie row

## Description

## Bug

On **iOS**, adding the **aiin.by** provider: the auth flow runs (loopback callback listener starts, browser sheet opens, sign-in completes on the page) — but **the AIIN provider never appears** in the providers list. Owner report (2026-09-28): «пытаюсь добавить aiin.by провайдер... прохожу auth flow но провайдер не добавляется. на ios». Owner rulings: AIIN «работает охрененно в браузере» (web reference behavior), and it must work exactly as well **on mobile and macOS** (app builds). Third ruling (2026-09-28, verbatim): «никаких фолбек на ключ... у нас там честный SSO должен быть... если что-то не получится то тогда надо будет мне в aiin.by адопшен запрашивать» — **no key-paste fallback at all; SSO is the only path**; if the SSO cannot be made to work client-side, the deliverable is a precise, evidence-backed adoption request for aiin.by (what to change on their side).

## Evidence (app log, iOS device, 2026-09-28)

```
11:33:03 [AIIN mobile] listening for the AIIN callback on http://127.0.0.1:65043/callback
11:33:32 [AIIN mobile] listening for the AIIN callback on http://127.0.0.1:65049/callback
11:33:35 [AIIN mobile] browser opened; sign in on the AIIN page
11:33:53 [Fa] reconfigure: baseUrl=https://codemie.lab.epam.com/code-assistant-api/v1,
           apiKey.len=190, isCodeMie=true, model.headers=[cookie]
11:33:58 [AIIN mobile] listening for the AIIN callback on http://127.0.0.1:65057/callback
```

Three listener starts (three Add taps), the browser sheet opened — and then **zero AIIN completion artifacts**: no model-picker push, no `[Fa] reconfigure` with `api.aiin.by`, no registry entry. The 11:33:53 reconfigure is **codemie** — see F4 below; it is NOT the AIIN flow (`_finishAiinConnect` always reconfigures with `aiinDefaultChatBaseUrl`).

## What the code does (read on origin/main; the local checkout predates this flow)

`flutter_app/lib/services/aiin_connect_flow.dart`:
- `runAiinConnectFlow` dispatches: web → `runAiinWebConnect` (the working popup path, #486); **mobile (iOS/Android) → `runAiinMobileConnect`** (#976); desktop → `_runAiinDesktopConnect`.
- `runAiinMobileConnect` runs the SAME loopback CLI server as desktop (`runAiinConnectCliFlow`, `lib/src/cli/aiin_connect_server.dart:152` logs the "listening" line) and opens the authorize URL in an **ASWebAuthenticationSession** sheet via the shared `fah/web_auth_session` MethodChannel (line ~311 — the same channel the CodeMie SSO flow drives).
- The design: the OAuth redirect (`http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback`) loads **inside the sheet**, hits the on-device server, `onCallback` dismisses the sheet, the server exchanges the code and returns `AiinConnectResult`.
- **`cancelWhenOpenSettles: authSession`** (iOS): the sheet resolving WITHOUT a server callback is treated as user cancel → `_completeAiinConnect` gets `result == null` → **silent paste-key fallback** (`_pasteAiinKeyFallback`). A user swipe and a lost race are indistinguishable by design.
- Success path: `_finishAiinConnect` → model picker from `api.aiin.by/v1/models` → registry entry named by account email → `service.reconfigure` (logs `baseUrl=api.aiin.by`).

## The CodeMie comparison (owner's pointer — decisive)

CodeMie SSO works on this exact iOS app through the SAME `fah/web_auth_session` channel. `AppDelegate.swift` (~lines 2284–2345) implements the native contract: `authenticate {url, callbackScheme}` creates the `ASWebAuthenticationSession`, **intercepts the redirect whose scheme matches `callbackScheme`** (iOS's RFC-8252 loopback interception), and **returns the callback URL to Dart**: `result(callbackURL?.absoluteString)` (or nil on user cancel).

CodeMie's Dart (`codemie_sso_flow.dart`, `systemAuthSessionCodeMieSso`) invokes it with **`callbackScheme: "http"`**, the redirect is `http://localhost:<port>/?token=...`, and the flow **consumes the returned URL** — extracting the token right out of it. WebView fallback only when the session cannot start.

AIIN's `_openAiinAuthSession` (aiin_connect_flow.dart ~319) breaks the contract in exactly two places:
1. **No `callbackScheme`** — it sends only `{'url': url}`; native reads `args["callbackScheme"]` → nil → **no interception**: the `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback` redirect becomes a plain in-sheet navigation, and the session's completion handler fires only on cancel.
2. **The return value is discarded** — `.then((_) => true)` throws the intercepted URL (when there is one) on the floor. CodeMie's flow builds its credentials from that URL; AIIN's Dart never looks at it.

So the flow's completion hinges entirely on the in-sheet navigation physically reaching the dart:io loopback server — the flakiest possible leg — while the proven mechanism (scheme interception + returned URL) sits one argument away. Owner's intuition confirmed: «и aiin.by тоже должна быть возможность легко получать это».

The AIIN provider definition is correct — `lib/src/providers/aiin_auth.dart:31-34` (`auth.aiin.by` / `api.aiin.by`); the endpoint hypothesis is **disproven** by code. The failure is in the mobile surface plumbing.

## Failure modes to discriminate (instrument first)

- **F2 — CONFIRMED wiring defect (primary)**: no `callbackScheme` in the `authenticate` call + the returned callback URL discarded (see the CodeMie comparison). With a nil scheme there is no interception; completion hinges on the in-sheet navigation reaching the dart:io server, and the race/cancel semantics (`cancelWhenOpenSettles`) then eat the flow. Fix is client-side: wire AIIN's session exactly like CodeMie's.
- **F1 — proxy blocks the redirect (remaining question)**: if the AIIN OAuth proxy refuses the `http://127.0.0.1` redirect target server-side (old code comment: «the AIIN proxy currently blocks cross-device redirects»), no redirect fires at all — sign-in completes, nothing comes back, which is also consistent with the owner log. After the F2 fix this is cleanly detectable as «no interception AND no navigation»; it is then the case for the AC8 aiin.by adoption request.
- **F3 — listener leak**: repeated taps stack loopback servers (three live listeners across one session, ports 65043/65049/65057) — the retry path starts a new flow without tearing down the previous one.
- **F4 — connection guard hijack (side observation)**: the 11:33:53 `reconfigure` to codemie is the boot/connection guard (`agent_service_connection_guard.dart`) restoring the last-saved connection when the app returned from the auth sheet — it mutates the active connection **in the middle of the AIIN add flow**. Not the root cause of the missing provider, but an I1-class violation that compounds the confusion.

## Fix contract (owner rulings: honest SSO, no paste fallback)

1. **iOS AIIN drives `fah/web_auth_session` with the CodeMie contract**: pass `callbackScheme: 'http'`, use the `localhost` redirect host (CodeMie's proven shape, replacing `127.0.0.1`), and **consume the callback URL the channel returns** — extract `code`/`state` and feed the flow's existing code-exchange. Completion must not depend on the in-sheet navigation reaching the dart:io server.
2. The dart:io loopback server stays the desktop/macOS mechanism (CLI parity) — untouched by the iOS fix.
3. If the AC2 instrumentation then shows the proxy never issues the redirect (F1), ship the AC8 aiin.by adoption spec; until anything works the flow fails visibly (I4).
4. F3: one loopback listener per attempt — Dart-side single flight.
5. F4: the connection guard never reconfigures the active connection while an add-provider flow is in progress.

## Invariants

- **I1** — An auth flow mutates exactly the provider row it started from; the connection guard never reconfigures the active connection while an add-provider flow is in progress (F4).
- **I2** — Single flight: one loopback listener per provider-add attempt; retries tear down the previous server (F3).
- **I3** — The shared `fah/web_auth_session` channel serves AIIN and CodeMie without cross-talk (both flows drive it; a CodeMie restore must not surface mid-AIIN).

2. **The return value is discarded** — `.then((_) => true)` throws the intercepted URL (when there is one) on the floor. CodeMie's flow builds its credentials from that URL; AIIN's Dart never looks at it.

So the flow's completion hinges entirely on the in-sheet navigation physically reaching the dart:io loopback server — the flakiest possible leg — while the proven mechanism (scheme interception + returned URL) sits one argument away. Owner's intuition confirmed: «и aiin.by тоже должна быть возможность легко получать это».

The AIIN provider definition is correct — `lib/src/providers/aiin_auth.dart:31-34` (`auth.aiin.by` / `api.aiin.by`); the endpoint hypothesis is **disproven** by code. The failure is in the mobile surface plumbing.

## Failure modes to discriminate (instrument first)

- **F2 — CONFIRMED wiring defect (primary)**: no `callbackScheme` in the `authenticate` call + the returned callback URL discarded (see the CodeMie comparison). With a nil scheme there is no interception; completion hinges on the in-sheet navigation reaching the dart:io server, and the race/cancel semantics (`cancelWhenOpenSettles`) then eat the flow. Fix is client-side: wire AIIN's session exactly like CodeMie's.
- **F1 — proxy blocks the redirect (remaining question)**: if the AIIN OAuth proxy refuses the `http://127.0.0.1` redirect target server-side (old code comment: «the AIIN proxy currently blocks cross-device redirects»), no redirect fires at all — sign-in completes, nothing comes back, which is also consistent with the owner log. After the F2 fix this is cleanly detectable as «no interception AND no navigation»; it is then the case for the AC8 aiin.by adoption request.
- **F3 — listener leak**: repeated taps stack loopback servers (three live listeners across one session, ports 65043/65049/65057) — the retry path starts a new flow without tearing down the previous one.
- **F4 — connection guard hijack (side observation)**: the 11:33:53 `reconfigure` to codemie is the boot/connection guard (`agent_service_connection_guard.dart`) restoring the last-saved connection when the app returned from the auth sheet — it mutates the active connection **in the middle of the AIIN add flow**. Not the root cause of the missing provider, but an I1-class violation that compounds the confusion.

## Fix contract (owner rulings: honest SSO, no paste fallback)

1. **iOS AIIN drives `fah/web_auth_session` with the CodeMie contract**: pass `callbackScheme: 'http'`, use the `localhost` redirect host (CodeMie's proven shape, replacing `127.0.0.1`), and **consume the callback URL the channel returns** — extract `code`/`state` and feed the flow's existing code-exchange. Completion must not depend on the in-sheet navigation reaching the dart:io server.
2. The dart:io loopback server stays the desktop/macOS mechanism (CLI parity) — untouched by the iOS fix.
3. If the AC2 instrumentation then shows the proxy never issues the redirect (F1), ship the AC8 aiin.by adoption spec; until anything works the flow fails visibly (I4).
4. F3: one loopback listener per attempt — Dart-side single flight.
5. F4: the connection guard never reconfigures the active connection while an add-provider flow is in progress.

## Invariants

- **I1** — An auth flow mutates exactly the provider row it started from; the connection guard never reconfigures the active connection while an add-provider flow is in progress (F4).
- **I2** — Single flight: one loopback listener per provider-add attempt; retries tear down the previous server (F3).
- **I3** — The shared `fah/web_auth_session` channel …

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/Step groups +
  collapsible turn/assistant-run summaries), `deriveTrajectoryTimeline`
  (four modes — `sequence` equal-width slots, `duration` with idle gaps
  compressed out, `time` zero-width wall-clock markers, `actual` real gaps;
  three fixed lanes: 0 system/user/context, 1 message/compacted, 2 tools),
  `trajectoryTimelineFocusIndexes` (selection → visible ledger indexes),
  and `ThrottledTrajectorySearchIndex` (full-text; matches are stable
  record ids). `formatters.dart` holds the shared duration/token/throughput
  formatting; `trajectory_preview.dart` the bounded single-line previews;
  `trajectory_export.dart` the whole-snapshot JSON/Markdown exporters the
  header's copy menu uses. Tool records carry `startedAt` (real launch
  time, distinct from the projected position) so the Gantt/actual
  projections plot true spans. Outbound model requests persist for the
  ledger as hidden `model_request_summary` `CustomRecord`s — the CLI
  event handler (`agent_event_handler.dart`, emitted through
  `agent_cli.dart`) and the app's `AgentService` both buffer a
  `TrajectoryRequestDetail` per call and flush it onto the session
  record chain right before the assistant message, so replays see it
  ahead of the reply — and `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder` folds them into
  the message record's request detail (the Request tab).
  Consumers render, never re-derive: `packages/fa_ui`'s
  `lib/src/trajectory/` widgets and the CLI `/trajectory` family.
- `lib/src/cli/trajectory_commands.dart` (a `part of` `agent_cli.dart`) +
  `lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart` — the read-only REPL family
  `/trajectory [view|cost|tail|inspect <n>]` (bare = `view`, capped at 200
  rows; `tail` follows the live session every 500ms) and the headless
  `fa trajectory <view|tail|cost|inspect> [sessionId] [--json] [--at N]`
  subcommand (`--at N` replays the snapshot as it stood at record N, view
  only). Session resolution: exact id > session-name match > most recent.
  Rendering is pure Dart in `trajectory_tui.dart` (no `dart:io`), shared by
  both entries; `bin/fah.dart` routes …

```dart
static Future _returnAsyncNotFuture(Object suspendState, Object? returnValue) {
  _Future future = ...;
  future._completeWithValue(returnValue);   // ← SYNCHRONOUS COMPLETION!
  return future;

```

An async function returning a non-Future value completes its future **SYNCHRONOUSLY** at the `return` statement (`_completeWithValue` — inline propagation of ALL listeners: `.then` callbacks AND await resumptions run RIGHT THERE).

Whereas `Completer.complete()` (an `_AsyncCompleter`) goes through `_asyncComplete` → `_asyncCompleteWithValue` → **`scheduleMicrotask`** — the listeners run in a LATER microtask!

So in `body`'s sync stretch:
1. `c.complete('x')` → schedules M_A (L1 runs in M_A, LATER).
2. `return` → `_completeWithValue` INLINE → `opened`'s listeners (L2, main's await) run RIGHT NOW.

Hence the observed order: L2, done, ..., L1. The async-fn return JUMPS THE QUEUE ahead of any completer completed earlier in the same stretch.

THIS EXPLAINS THE FLOW BUG PERFECTLY:

In the mobile openBrowserFn wrapper:
```dart
(url) async {
  final callbackUrl = await _openAiinAuthSession(url);   // sheet resolves
  if (intercepted != null && !intercepted.isCompleted) {
    intercepted.complete(callbackUrl);   // → schedules intercepted.then as MICROTASK M_A
  }
  return true;                            // → SYNCHRONOUS propagation!
}
```

`return true` synchronously completes the wrapper's future → `_openAiinBrowser`'s `await openBrowserFn(...)` resumption — wait, is the await resumption synchronous too?? `await future` where future is ALREADY complete → `_awaitCompletedFuture` → `future._zone.scheduleMicrotask(run)` — SCHEDULED. Hmm — but the await was attached when the future was INCOMPLETE → `_thenAwait` → a listener on the wrapper's future → `_completeWithValue` propagates listeners inline → the listener is the _SuspendState thenCallback wrapper → `zone.runUnary(_thenCallback, value)` — hmm, `_thenAwait` registers `_thenCallback` directly as a listener — `_completeWithValue` → `_propagateToListeners` → handleValueCallback → `listener.handleValue(sourceResult)` → calls `_thenCallback(value)` = `suspendState._resume(value, ...)` — **the await resumption runs INLINE, synchronously!**

So at `return true`:
- INLINE: _openAiinBrowser resumes: `onStatus('browser opened...')` → `_openAiinBrowser` returns → its own future completes via `_returnAsyncNotFuture` → **INLINE again**: `opened`'s listeners:
  - the guard `opened.then(...)` in `_firstCallbackOrOpenError` → runs INLINE: `cancelWhenOpenSettles=true`, `surfaceClosed` not completed, **`interceptedCallback` NOT completed** (M_A hasn't run yet — it's just queued!) → **`surfaceClosed.completeError(AiinSurfaceClosedException())`** ← THE BUG!

- Then the event loop drains M_A: intercepted.then fires → url != null → interceptedCallback.complete — TOO LATE, the race already resolved with the surfaceClosed error.

CONFIRMED ROOT CAUSE — the race in `_firstCallbackOrOpenError` loses because:
1. `intercepted.complete(url)` schedules its `.then` listener as a MICROTASK (async completer).
2. The wrapper's `return true` SYNCHRONOUSLY cascades: wrapper future → _openAiinBrowser await resumption → onStatus → _openAiinBrowser's own return → `opened`'s completion (synchronous) → the `cancelWhenOpenSettles` guard runs IMMEDIATELY, BEFORE the queued intercepted listener ever gets a chance.
3. The guard's `interceptedCallback.isCompleted` check is FALSE → surfaceClosed wins → the flow cancels despite the intercepted URL being in hand.

The design comment "Completing it BEFORE the open future's bool keeps the flow's race order" was based on the WRONG microtask model — async-fn returns complete SYNCHRONOUSLY (this changed in Dart ~2.17+ when `_returnAsyncNotFuture` switched from `_asyncCompleteWithValue` to `_completeWithValue` for perf).

The race then delivers via M_B (interceptedCallback listener). CORRECT.

But fragile — relies on subtle scheduling again. 

**Option B (server-side, root cause)**: the RACE itself should not treat "open settled" as cancel when an intercepted callback is still pending. The `intercepted` FUTURE being pending ≠ no callback coming. The real semantics: `cancelWhenOpenSettles` exists for the sheet that closed WITHOUT delivering a callback. But in the new AC9 contract, the SAME `authenticate` call delivers BOTH the open-settle AND the callback URL through `intercepted`. When `intercepted != null`, the "open settled without callback" signal is EXACTLY the intercepted future resolving with NULL — the `opened` settle is redundant for the auth-session surface!

Look at the wiring: for authSession, openBrowserFn completes when the SHEET RESOLVES (the await on _openAiinAuthSession), and intercepted completes from the same resolution. The `opened` completion carries NO extra information — the intercepted future is the sheet's completion value. So under the AC9 contract, `cancelWhenOpenSettles` + `opened`-settle-guard is a DUPLICATE cancel path racing (and losing) against the intercepted delivery.

Cleanest root fix in `runAiinConnectCliFlow` / `_firstCallbackOrOpenError`: when an `intercepted` future exists, the `opened` settle must NOT trigger the cancel — the intercepted future's own null resolution is the cancel signal. `cancelWhenOpenSettles` then only applies when `intercepted == null` (an external-browser surface... but wait — cancelWhenOpenSettles was introduced exactly FOR the auth-session; desktop leaves it false).

With Option B, the guard on `opened` would be skipped entirely when intercepted != null — the cancel comes solely from intercepted == null. Same semantics, no race, and the redundant path is gone. With the guard skipped (intercepted != null), the flow would wait for the intercepted future... whic…

1. `intercepted.complete(url)` — queues its listener as a microtask
2. `return true` — **synchronously** cascades: wrapper future → `_openAiinBrowser` resumes → `opened` completes → the `cancelWhenOpenSettles` guard runs **inline, before the queued intercepted listener** → guard sees `interceptedCallback` incomplete → `AiinSurfaceClosedException` wins the race

The `opened`-settle cancel path duplicates the intercepted future's own cancel signal (both come from the same sheet resolution) and always beats it due to this scheduling asymmetry. # GitHub tracker comment

Use GitHub-flavored Markdown in `outputs/response.md` for GitHub issue
comments and descriptions. Your output is posted to the issue as-is — every
construct must render natively on GitHub.

- Headings: `##`, `###`
- Bullets: `- item`
- Numbered lists: `1. item`
- Bold: `**text**`
- Inline code: `` `code` ``
- Code block: ` ```lang ... ``` ` with a language tag (`dart`, `bash`, `json`)
- Link: `[text](url)`
- Tables: standard GFM table syntax (`|---|` separator row)

Do not use Jira wiki markup in GitHub fields: no `{code}...{code}` blocks,
no `{panel}` macros, no `h1.`/`h2.`/`h3.` heading prefixes, no
`{{monospace}}` inline code, no `[title|url]` links. None of it renders on
GitHub — a comment full of `{code}` fences and `h3.` headers is unreadable.

**IMPORTANT** When the issue references a parent story or related issues,
get them for full context using: `dmtools github_get_issue OWNER/REPO#NUMBER`
(the composite key form works directly).
