68:## Acceptance criteria
70:- **AC1** — iOS: complete AIIN sign-in → provider row created (endpoint api.aiin.by), model picker appears, `reconfigure` logs `baseUrl=api.aiin.by`; the row is selectable per-session.
71:- **AC2** — Instrumentation: the flow logs server `/callback` hits, sheet resolution and the cancel-race outcome — F1 vs F2 is answerable from logs alone (owner's repro scenario reproducible).
72:- **AC3** — Retry while a flow is active reuses one listener; the log shows at most one live loopback server per add attempt.
73:- **AC4** — Cancel/timeout/failure produces a **visible error state** (no paste sheet, no silent exit): what happened + the AC2 diagnostic bundle (callback hit? sheet resolution? race outcome) — widget/VM test on `result == null` and on sheet-settles-first.
74:- **AC5** — macOS app build: the add flow completes end-to-end the same way (desktop loopback + external browser is the same code the CLI `/provider aiin` uses — app E2E proves the wiring).

# gh-1044: [BUG] iOS/MACos: AIIN (aiin.by) provider add — auth flow completes but provider never added; reconfigure binds to the CodeMie row

## Description

## Bug

On **iOS**, adding the **aiin.by** provider: the auth flow runs (loopback callback listener starts, browser sheet opens, sign-in completes on the page) — but **the AIIN provider never appears** in the providers list. Owner report (2026-09-28): «пытаюсь добавить aiin.by провайдер... прохожу auth flow но провайдер не добавляется. на ios». Owner rulings: AIIN «работает охрененно в браузере» (web reference behavior), and it must work exactly as well **on mobile and macOS** (app builds). Third ruling (2026-09-28, verbatim): «никаких фолбек на ключ... у нас там честный SSO должен быть... если что-то не получится то тогда надо будет мне в aiin.by адопшен запрашивать» — **no key-paste fallback at all; SSO is the only path**; if the SSO cannot be made to work client-side, the deliverable is a precise, evidence-backed adoption request for aiin.by (what to change on their side).

## Evidence (app log, iOS device, 2026-09-28)

```
11:33:03 [AIIN mobile] listening for the AIIN callback on http://127.0.0.1:65043/callback
11:33:32 [AIIN mobile] listening for the AIIN callback on http://127.0.0.1:65049/callback
11:33:35 [AIIN mobile] browser opened; sign in on the AIIN page
11:33:53 [Fa] reconfigure: baseUrl=https://codemie.lab.epam.com/code-assistant-api/v1,
           apiKey.len=190, isCodeMie=true, model.headers=[cookie]
11:33:58 [AIIN mobile] listening for the AIIN callback on http://127.0.0.1:65057/callback
```

Three listener starts (three Add taps), the browser sheet opened — and then **zero AIIN completion artifacts**: no model-picker push, no `[Fa] reconfigure` with `api.aiin.by`, no registry entry. The 11:33:53 reconfigure is **codemie** — see F4 below; it is NOT the AIIN flow (`_finishAiinConnect` always reconfigures with `aiinDefaultChatBaseUrl`).

## What the code does (read on origin/main; the local checkout predates this flow)

`flutter_app/lib/services/aiin_connect_flow.dart`:
- `runAiinConnectFlow` dispatches: web → `runAiinWebConnect` (the working popup path, #486); **mobile (iOS/Android) → `runAiinMobileConnect`** (#976); desktop → `_runAiinDesktopConnect`.
- `runAiinMobileConnect` runs the SAME loopback CLI server as desktop (`runAiinConnectCliFlow`, `lib/src/cli/aiin_connect_server.dart:152` logs the "listening" line) and opens the authorize URL in an **ASWebAuthenticationSession** sheet via the shared `fah/web_auth_session` MethodChannel (line ~311 — the same channel the CodeMie SSO flow drives).
- The design: the OAuth redirect (`http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback`) loads **inside the sheet**, hits the on-device server, `onCallback` dismisses the sheet, the server exchanges the code and returns `AiinConnectResult`.
- **`cancelWhenOpenSettles: authSession`** (iOS): the sheet resolving WITHOUT a server callback is treated as user cancel → `_completeAiinConnect` gets `result == null` → **silent paste-key fallback** (`_pasteAiinKeyFallback`). A user swipe and a lost race are indistinguishable by design.
- Success path: `_finishAiinConnect` → model picker from `api.aiin.by/v1/models` → registry entry named by account email → `service.reconfigure` (logs `baseUrl=api.aiin.by`).

## The CodeMie comparison (owner's pointer — decisive)

CodeMie SSO works on this exact iOS app through the SAME `fah/web_auth_session` channel. `AppDelegate.swift` (~lines 2284–2345) implements the native contract: `authenticate {url, callbackScheme}` creates the `ASWebAuthenticationSession`, **intercepts the redirect whose scheme matches `callbackScheme`** (iOS's RFC-8252 loopback interception), and **returns the callback URL to Dart**: `result(callbackURL?.absoluteString)` (or nil on user cancel).

CodeMie's Dart (`codemie_sso_flow.dart`, `systemAuthSessionCodeMieSso`) invokes it with **`callbackScheme: "http"`**, the redirect is `http://localhost:<port>/?token=...`, and the flow **consumes the returned URL** — extracting the token right out of it. WebView fallback only when the session cannot start.

AIIN's `_openAiinAuthSession` (aiin_connect_flow.dart ~319) breaks the contract in exactly two places:
1. **No `callbackScheme`** — it sends only `{'url': url}`; native reads `args["callbackScheme"]` → nil → **no interception**: the `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback` redirect becomes a plain in-sheet navigation, and the session's completion handler fires only on cancel.
2. **The return value is discarded** — `.then((_) => true)` throws the intercepted URL (when there is one) on the floor. CodeMie's flow builds its credentials from that URL; AIIN's Dart never looks at it.

  listener on 'localhost' (RFC 8252 §4.1 — iOS only auto-intercepts the
  localhost host form), consume the callback URL returned by the channel and
  feed it to the CLI server's onCallback through a scoped HttpOverrides
  localhost alias, and treat a sheet resolution without a callback as a
  visible error (no paste fallback).
- aiin_connect_server.dart: single-flight latch (retry reuses the live
  listener), cancellation that survives a same-microtask complete-then-close
  race (the close guard ran in the openFuture's microtask before the future
  could be awaited — close() while adding the stream threw
  'Cannot close sink while adding stream'), and /callback + race logging so
  F1 (proxy never redirects) is answerable from logs.
- agent_service.dart / relay_agent_service.dart: reconfigure awaits the
  in-flight connect (parity with the guard fix in #327) so the AIIN
  reconfigure can no longer be hijacked by the codemie row (F4).
- tests: mobile VM tests drive runAiinMobileConnect with an iOS override and
  the mocked channel (callback-lands success, cannot-start and
  sheet-settles-first visible errors, double-tap single listener, android
  parity); step tests gain the desktop-hop teardown-safe host; server tests
  cover the latch, the close race, provider error callbacks and timeouts." && git log --oneline -1

session never intercepted the http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback redirect) and
the intercepted callback URL was discarded (.then((_)). The sheet therefore
resolved without a callback every time, which the flow treated as a silent
paste-key fallback — no provider, no error.

  listener on 'localhost' (RFC 8252 §4.1 — iOS only auto-intercepts the
  localhost host form), consume the callback URL returned by the channel and
  feed it to the CLI server's onCallback through a scoped HttpOverrides
  localhost alias, and treat a sheet resolution without a callback as a
  visible error (no paste fallback).
- aiin_connect_server.dart: single-flight latch (retry reuses the live
  listener), cancellation that survives a same-microtask complete-then-close
  race (the close guard ran in the openFuture's microtask before the future
  could be awaited — close() while adding the stream threw
  'Cannot close sink while adding stream'), and /callback + race logging so
  F1 (proxy never redirects) is answerable from logs.
- agent_service.dart / relay_agent_service.dart: reconfigure awaits the
  in-flight connect (parity with the guard fix in #327) so the AIIN
  reconfigure can no longer be hijacked by the codemie row (F4).
- tests: mobile VM tests drive runAiinMobileConnect with an iOS override and
  the mocked channel (callback-lands success, cannot-start and
  sheet-settles-first visible errors, double-tap single listener, android
  parity); step tests gain the desktop-hop teardown-safe host; server tests
  cover the latch, the close race, provider error callbacks and timeouts." && git log --oneline -1

# gh-1044: [BUG] iOS/MACos: AIIN (aiin.by) provider add — auth flow completes but provider never added; reconfigure binds to the CodeMie row

## Description

## Bug

On **iOS**, adding the **aiin.by** provider: the auth flow runs (loopback callback listener starts, browser sheet opens, sign-in completes on the page) — but **the AIIN provider never appears** in the providers list. Owner report (2026-09-28): «пытаюсь добавить aiin.by провайдер... прохожу auth flow но провайдер не добавляется. на ios». Owner rulings: AIIN «работает охрененно в браузере» (web reference behavior), and it must work exactly as well **on mobile and macOS** (app builds). Third ruling (2026-09-28, verbatim): «никаких фолбек на ключ... у нас там честный SSO должен быть... если что-то не получится то тогда надо будет мне в aiin.by адопшен запрашивать» — **no key-paste fallback at all; SSO is the only path**; if the SSO cannot be made to work client-side, the deliverable is a precise, evidence-backed adoption request for aiin.by (what to change on their side).

## Evidence (app log, iOS device, 2026-09-28)

```
11:33:03 [AIIN mobile] listening for the AIIN callback on http://127.0.0.1:65043/callback
11:33:32 [AIIN mobile] listening for the AIIN callback on http://127.0.0.1:65049/callback
11:33:35 [AIIN mobile] browser opened; sign in on the AIIN page
11:33:53 [Fa] reconfigure: baseUrl=https://codemie.lab.epam.com/code-assistant-api/v1,
           apiKey.len=190, isCodeMie=true, model.headers=[cookie]
11:33:58 [AIIN mobile] listening for the AIIN callback on http://127.0.0.1:65057/callback
```

Three listener starts (three Add taps), the browser sheet opened — and then **zero AIIN completion artifacts**: no model-picker push, no `[Fa] reconfigure` with `api.aiin.by`, no registry entry. The 11:33:53 reconfigure is **codemie** — see F4 below; it is NOT the AIIN flow (`_finishAiinConnect` always reconfigures with `aiinDefaultChatBaseUrl`).

## What the code does (read on origin/main; the local checkout predates this flow)

`flutter_app/lib/services/aiin_connect_flow.dart`:
- `runAiinConnectFlow` dispatches: web → `runAiinWebConnect` (the working popup path, #486); **mobile (iOS/Android) → `runAiinMobileConnect`** (#976); desktop → `_runAiinDesktopConnect`.
- `runAiinMobileConnect` runs the SAME loopback CLI server as desktop (`runAiinConnectCliFlow`, `lib/src/cli/aiin_connect_server.dart:152` logs the "listening" line) and opens the authorize URL in an **ASWebAuthenticationSession** sheet via the shared `fah/web_auth_session` MethodChannel (line ~311 — the same channel the CodeMie SSO flow drives).
- The design: the OAuth redirect (`http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback`) loads **inside the sheet**, hits the on-device server, `onCallback` dismisses the sheet, the server exchanges the code and returns `AiinConnectResult`.
- **`cancelWhenOpenSettles: authSession`** (iOS): the sheet resolving WITHOUT a server callback is treated as user cancel → `_completeAiinConnect` gets `result == null` → **silent paste-key fallback** (`_pasteAiinKeyFallback`). A user swipe and a lost race are indistinguishable by design.
- Success path: `_finishAiinConnect` → model picker from `api.aiin.by/v1/models` → registry entry named by account email → `service.reconfigure` (logs `baseUrl=api.aiin.by`).

## The CodeMie comparison (owner's pointer — decisive)

CodeMie SSO works on this exact iOS app through the SAME `fah/web_auth_session` channel. `AppDelegate.swift` (~lines 2284–2345) implements the native contract: `authenticate {url, callbackScheme}` creates the `ASWebAuthenticationSession`, **intercepts the redirect whose scheme matches `callbackScheme`** (iOS's RFC-8252 loopback interception), and **returns the callback URL to Dart**: `result(callbackURL?.absoluteString)` (or nil on user cancel).

CodeMie's Dart (`codemie_sso_flow.dart`, `systemAuthSessionCodeMieSso`) invokes it with **`callbackScheme: "http"`**, the redirect is `http://localhost:<port>/?token=...`, and the flow **consumes the returned URL** — extracting the token right out of it. WebView fallback only when the session cannot start.

AIIN's `_openAiinAuthSession` (aiin_connect_flow.dart ~319) breaks the contract in exactly two places:
1. **No `callbackScheme`** — it sends only `{'url': url}`; native reads `args["callbackScheme"]` → nil → **no interception**: the `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback` redirect becomes a plain in-sheet navigation, and the session's completion handler fires only on cancel.
2. **The return value is discarded** — `.then((_) => true)` throws the intercepted URL (when there is one) on the floor. CodeMie's flow builds its credentials from that URL; AIIN's Dart never looks at it.

## Root cause

The iOS/macOS AIIN add-provider flow broke the shared `fah/web_auth_session` contract that CodeMie's working SSO flow honors, in two places (`_openAiinAuthSession`):

1. **No `callbackScheme` argument** — the native `ASWebAuthenticationSession` only intercepts the redirect when the requested scheme matches `callbackScheme`. AIIN sent only `{'url': ...}`, so the `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback` redirect became a plain in-sheet navigation and the session's completion handler fired only on user cancel.
2. **The intercepted callback URL was discarded** (`.then((_) => true)`) — CodeMie's flow builds its credentials from that URL; AIIN's Dart never looked at it.

Compounding factors:

- the loopback listener bound on `127.0.0.1` while iOS auto-intercepts only the `localhost` host form (RFC 8252 §4.1) — even with interception, the redirect never matched the server URL the browser was told to hit;
- a sheet resolution without a callback was treated as a user cancel → **silent paste-key fallback**, so the failure was invisible (owner ruling: no paste fallback, honest SSO only);
- `service.reconfigure` did not await the in-flight connect, letting the last-saved codemie row's reconfigure land after AIIN's (the 11:33:53 `baseUrl=codemie...` in the owner's log, F4);
- the CLI server's `close()` guard ran in `openFuture`'s microtask, so a same-microtask complete-then-close (cancel timeout, double tap) threw `Bad state: Cannot close sink while adding stream`.

## Fix

- `aiin_connect_flow.dart`: pass `callbackScheme: 'http'`, bind on `localhost`, consume the callback URL returned by the channel and feed it to the CLI server's `onCallback` through a scoped `HttpOverrides` localhost alias, visible error on sheet-resolves-without-callback.
- `aiin_connect_server.dart`: single-flight latch, race-safe close, `/callback` + cancel-race logging (F1 vs F2 answerable from logs).
- `agent_service.dart` / `relay_agent_service.dart`: `reconfigure` awaits the in-flight connect (parity with #327).

## Tests

- mobile VM tests drive `runAiinMobileConnect` with an iOS override + mocked channel: callback-lands → success (model picker + registry + aiin reconfigure), cannot-start and sheet-settles-first → visible snack errors, double-tap → single listener, android parity.
- desktop-hop step tests made teardown-safe (real-async server binds inside `runAsync`).
- server tests: latch reuse, close-race, provider error callback surfacing, cancel/timeout.

64 flutter tests + 16 dart tests pass; no new analyzer issues.
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -2

## Root cause

The iOS/macOS AIIN add-provider flow broke the shared `fah/web_auth_session` contract that CodeMie's working SSO flow honors, in two places (`_openAiinAuthSession`):

1. **No `callbackScheme` argument** — the native `ASWebAuthenticationSession` only intercepts the redirect when the requested scheme matches `callbackScheme`. AIIN sent only `{'url': ...}`, so the `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback` redirect became a plain in-sheet navigation and the session's completion handler fired only on user cancel.
2. **The intercepted callback URL was discarded** (`.then((_) => true)`) — CodeMie's flow builds its credentials from that URL; AIIN's Dart never looked at it.

Compounding factors:

- the loopback listener bound on `127.0.0.1` while iOS auto-intercepts only the `localhost` host form (RFC 8252 §4.1) — even with interception, the redirect never matched the server URL the browser was told to hit;
- a sheet resolution without a callback was treated as a user cancel → **silent paste-key fallback**, so the failure was invisible (owner ruling: no paste fallback, honest SSO only);
- `service.reconfigure` did not await the in-flight connect, letting the last-saved codemie row's reconfigure land after AIIN's (the 11:33:53 `baseUrl=codemie...` in the owner's log, F4);
- the CLI server's `close()` guard ran in `openFuture`'s microtask, so a same-microtask complete-then-close (cancel timeout, double tap) threw `Bad state: Cannot close sink while adding stream`.

## Fix

- `aiin_connect_flow.dart`: pass `callbackScheme: 'http'`, bind on `localhost`, consume the callback URL returned by the channel and feed it to the CLI server's `onCallback` through a scoped `HttpOverrides` localhost alias, visible error on sheet-resolves-without-callback.
- `aiin_connect_server.dart`: single-flight latch, race-safe close, `/callback` + cancel-race logging (F1 vs F2 answerable from logs).

- desktop-hop step tests made teardown-safe (real-async server binds inside `runAsync`).
- server tests: latch reuse, close-race, provider error callback surfacing, cancel/timeout.

64 flutter tests + 16 dart tests pass; no new analyzer issues.

## Root cause

The iOS/macOS AIIN add-provider flow broke the shared `fah/web_auth_session` contract that CodeMie's working SSO flow honors, in two places (`_openAiinAuthSession`):

1. **No `callbackScheme` argument** — the native `ASWebAuthenticationSession` only intercepts the redirect when the requested scheme matches `callbackScheme`. AIIN sent only `{'url': ...}`, so the `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback` redirect became a plain in-sheet navigation and the session's completion handler fired only on user cancel.
2. **The intercepted callback URL was discarded** (`.then((_) => true)`) — CodeMie's flow builds its credentials from that URL; AIIN's Dart never looked at it.

Compounding factors:

- the loopback listener bound on `127.0.0.1` while iOS auto-intercepts only the `localhost` host form (RFC 8252 §4.1) — even with interception, the redirect never matched the server URL the browser was told to hit;
- a sheet resolution without a callback was treated as a user cancel → **silent paste-key fallback**, so the failure was invisible (owner ruling: no paste fallback, honest SSO only);
- `service.reconfigure` did not await the in-flight connect, letting the last-saved codemie row's reconfigure land after AIIN's (the 11:33:53 `baseUrl=codemie...` in the owner's log, F4);
- the CLI server's `close()` guard ran in `openFuture`'s microtask, so a same-microtask complete-then-close (cancel timeout, double tap) threw `Bad state: Cannot close sink while adding stream`.

## Fix

- `aiin_connect_flow.dart`: pass `callbackScheme: 'http'`, bind on `localhost`, consume the callback URL returned by the channel and feed it to the CLI server's `onCallback` through a scoped `HttpOverrides` localhost alias, visible error on sheet-resolves-without-callback.
- `aiin_connect_server.dart`: single-flight latch, race-safe close, `/callback` + cancel-race logging (F1 vs F2 answerable from logs).
- `agent_service.dart` / `relay_agent_service.dart`: `reconfigure` awaits the in-flight connect (parity with #327).

## Tests

- mobile VM tests drive `runAiinMobileConnect` with an iOS override + mocked channel: callback-lands → success (model picker + registry + aiin reconfigure), cannot-start and sheet-settles-first → visible snack errors, double-tap → single listener, android parity.
- desktop-hop step tests made teardown-safe (real-async server binds inside `runAsync`).
- server tests: latch reuse, close-race, provider error callback surfacing, cancel/timeout.

64 flutter tests + 16 dart tests pass; no new analyzer issues.
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -2

# gh-1044: [BUG] iOS/MACos: AIIN (aiin.by) provider add — auth flow completes but provider never added; reconfigure binds to the CodeMie row

## Description

## Bug

On **iOS**, adding the **aiin.by** provider: the auth flow runs (loopback callback listener starts, browser sheet opens, sign-in completes on the page) — but **the AIIN provider never appears** in the providers list. Owner report (2026-09-28): «пытаюсь добавить aiin.by провайдер... прохожу auth flow но провайдер не добавляется. на ios». Owner rulings: AIIN «работает охрененно в браузере» (web reference behavior), and it must work exactly as well **on mobile and macOS** (app builds). Third ruling (2026-09-28, verbatim): «никаких фолбек на ключ... у нас там честный SSO должен быть... если что-то не получится то тогда надо будет мне в aiin.by адопшен запрашивать» — **no key-paste fallback at all; SSO is the only path**; if the SSO cannot be made to work client-side, the deliverable is a precise, evidence-backed adoption request for aiin.by (what to change on their side).

## Evidence (app log, iOS device, 2026-09-28)

```
11:33:03 [AIIN mobile] listening for the AIIN callback on http://127.0.0.1:65043/callback
11:33:32 [AIIN mobile] listening for the AIIN callback on http://127.0.0.1:65049/callback
11:33:35 [AIIN mobile] browser opened; sign in on the AIIN page
11:33:53 [Fa] reconfigure: baseUrl=https://codemie.lab.epam.com/code-assistant-api/v1,
           apiKey.len=190, isCodeMie=true, model.headers=[cookie]
11:33:58 [AIIN mobile] listening for the AIIN callback on http://127.0.0.1:65057/callback
```

Three listener starts (three Add taps), the browser sheet opened — and then **zero AIIN completion artifacts**: no model-picker push, no `[Fa] reconfigure` with `api.aiin.by`, no registry entry. The 11:33:53 reconfigure is **codemie** — see F4 below; it is NOT the AIIN flow (`_finishAiinConnect` always reconfigures with `aiinDefaultChatBaseUrl`).

## What the code does (read on origin/main; the local checkout predates this flow)

`flutter_app/lib/services/aiin_connect_flow.dart`:
- `runAiinConnectFlow` dispatches: web → `runAiinWebConnect` (the working popup path, #486); **mobile (iOS/Android) → `runAiinMobileConnect`** (#976); desktop → `_runAiinDesktopConnect`.
- `runAiinMobileConnect` runs the SAME loopback CLI server as desktop (`runAiinConnectCliFlow`, `lib/src/cli/aiin_connect_server.dart:152` logs the "listening" line) and opens the authorize URL in an **ASWebAuthenticationSession** sheet via the shared `fah/web_auth_session` MethodChannel (line ~311 — the same channel the CodeMie SSO flow drives).
- The design: the OAuth redirect (`http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback`) loads **inside the sheet**, hits the on-device server, `onCallback` dismisses the sheet, the server exchanges the code and returns `AiinConnectResult`.
- **`cancelWhenOpenSettles: authSession`** (iOS): the sheet resolving WITHOUT a server callback is treated as user cancel → `_completeAiinConnect` gets `result == null` → **silent paste-key fallback** (`_pasteAiinKeyFallback`). A user swipe and a lost race are indistinguishable by design.
- Success path: `_finishAiinConnect` → model picker from `api.aiin.by/v1/models` → registry entry named by account email → `service.reconfigure` (logs `baseUrl=api.aiin.by`).

## The CodeMie comparison (owner's pointer — decisive)

CodeMie SSO works on this exact iOS app through the SAME `fah/web_auth_session` channel. `AppDelegate.swift` (~lines 2284–2345) implements the native contract: `authenticate {url, callbackScheme}` creates the `ASWebAuthenticationSession`, **intercepts the redirect whose scheme matches `callbackScheme`** (iOS's RFC-8252 loopback interception), and **returns the callback URL to Dart**: `result(callbackURL?.absoluteString)` (or nil on user cancel).

CodeMie's Dart (`codemie_sso_flow.dart`, `systemAuthSessionCodeMieSso`) invokes it with **`callbackScheme: "http"`**, the redirect is `http://localhost:<port>/?token=...`, and the flow **consumes the returned URL** — extracting the token right out of it. WebView fallback only when the session cannot start.

AIIN's `_openAiinAuthSession` (aiin_connect_flow.dart ~319) breaks the contract in exactly two places:
1. **No `callbackScheme`** — it sends only `{'url': url}`; native reads `args["callbackScheme"]` → nil → **no interception**: the `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback` redirect becomes a plain in-sheet navigation, and the session's completion handler fires only on cancel.
2. **The return value is discarded** — `.then((_) => true)` throws the intercepted URL (when there is one) on the floor. CodeMie's flow builds its credentials from that URL; AIIN's Dart never looks at it.

{"command":"git push -q origin ai/gh-1044 2>&1 | tail -2; gh pr create --title "fix(#1044): AIIN mobile/macOS add-provider — sign-in completes but the provider is never added" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Root cause

The iOS/macOS AIIN add-provider flow broke the shared `fah/web_auth_session` contract that CodeMie's working SSO flow honors, in two places (`_openAiinAuthSession`):

1. **No `callbackScheme` argument** — the native `ASWebAuthenticationSession` only intercepts the redirect when the requested scheme matches `callbackScheme`. AIIN sent only `{'url': ...}`, so the `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback` redirect became a plain in-sheet navigation and the session's completion handler fired only on user cancel.
2. **The intercepted callback URL was discarded** (`.then((_) => true)`) — CodeMie's flow builds its credentials from that URL; AIIN's Dart never looked at it.

Compounding factors:

- the loopback listener bound on `127.0.0.1` while iOS auto-intercepts only the `localhost` host form (RFC 8252 §4.1) — even with interception, the redirect never matched the server URL the browser was told to hit;
- a sheet resolution without a callback was treated as a user cancel → **silent paste-key fallback**, so the failure was invisible (owner ruling: no paste fallback, honest SSO only);
- `service.reconfigure` did not await the in-flight connect, letting the last-saved codemie row's reconfigure land after AIIN's (the 11:33:53 `baseUrl=codemie...` in the owner's log, F4);
- the CLI server's `close()` guard ran in `openFuture`'s microtask, so a same-microtask complete-then-close (cancel timeout, double tap) threw `Bad state: Cannot close sink while adding stream`.

## Fix

- `aiin_connect_flow.dart`: pass `callbackScheme: 'http'`, bind on `localhost`, consume the callback URL returned by the channel and feed it to the CLI server's `onCallback` through a scoped `HttpOverrides` localhost alias, visible error on sheet-resolves-without-callback.
- `aiin_connect_server.dart`: single-flight latch, race-safe close, `/callback` + cancel-race logging (F1 vs F2 answerable from logs).
- `agent_service.dart` / `relay_agent_service.dart`: `reconfigure` awaits the in-flight connect (parity with #327).

## Tests

- mobile VM tests drive `runAiinMobileConnect` with an iOS override + mocked channel: callback-lands → success (model picker + registry + aiin reconfigure), cannot-start and sheet-settles-first → visible snack errors, double-tap → single listener, android parity.
- desktop-hop step tests made teardown-safe (real-async server binds inside `runAsync`).
- server tests: latch reuse, close-race, provider error callback surfacing, cancel/timeout.

64 flutter tests + 16 dart tests pass; no new analyzer issues.
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -2","timeout":120}

## Root cause

The iOS/macOS AIIN add-provider flow broke the shared `fah/web_auth_session` contract that CodeMie's working SSO flow honors, in two places (`_openAiinAuthSession`):

1. **No `callbackScheme` argument** — the native `ASWebAuthenticationSession` only intercepts the redirect when the requested scheme matches `callbackScheme`. AIIN sent only `{'url': ...}`, so the `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback` redirect became a plain in-sheet navigation and the session's completion handler fired only on user cancel.
2. **The intercepted callback URL was discarded** (`.then((_) => true)`) — CodeMie's flow builds its credentials from that URL; AIIN's Dart never looked at it.

Compounding factors:

- the loopback listener bound on `127.0.0.1` while iOS auto-intercepts only the `localhost` host form (RFC 8252 §4.1) — even with interception, the redirect never matched the server URL the browser was told to hit;
- a sheet resolution without a callback was treated as a user cancel → **silent paste-key fallback**, so the failure was invisible (owner ruling: no paste fallback, honest SSO only);
- `service.reconfigure` did not await the in-flight connect, letting the last-saved codemie row's reconfigure land after AIIN's (the 11:33:53 `baseUrl=codemie...` in the owner's log, F4);
- the CLI server's `close()` guard ran in `openFuture`'s microtask, so a same-microtask complete-then-close (cancel timeout, double tap) threw `Bad state: Cannot close sink while adding stream`.

## Fix

- `aiin_connect_flow.dart`: pass `callbackScheme: 'http'`, bind on `localhost`, consume the callback URL returned by the channel and feed it to the CLI server's `onCallback` through a scoped `HttpOverrides` localhost alias, visible error on sheet-resolves-without-callback.
- `aiin_connect_server.dart`: single-flight latch, race-safe close, `/callback` + cancel-race logging (F1 vs F2 answerable from logs).
- `agent_service.dart` / `relay_agent_service.dart`: `reconfigure` awaits the in-flight connect (parity with #327).

## Tests

- mobile VM tests drive `runAiinMobileConnect` with an iOS override + mocked channel: callback-lands → success (model picker + registry + aiin reconfigure), cannot-start and sheet-settles-first → visible snack errors, double-tap → single listener, android parity.
- desktop-hop step tests made teardown-safe (real-async server binds inside `runAsync`).
- server tests: latch reuse, close-race, provider error callback surfacing, cancel/timeout.

64 flutter tests + 16 dart tests pass; no new analyzer issues.

## Root cause

The iOS/macOS AIIN add-provider flow broke the shared `fah/web_auth_session` contract that CodeMie's working SSO flow honors, in two places (`_openAiinAuthSession`):

1. **No `callbackScheme` argument** — the native `ASWebAuthenticationSession` only intercepts the redirect when the requested scheme matches `callbackScheme`. AIIN sent only `{'url': ...}`, so the `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback` redirect became a plain in-sheet navigation and the session's completion handler fired only on user cancel.
2. **The intercepted callback URL was discarded** (`.then((_) => true)`) — CodeMie's flow builds its credentials from that URL; AIIN's Dart never looked at it.

Compounding factors:

- the loopback listener bound on `127.0.0.1` while iOS auto-intercepts only the `localhost` host form (RFC 8252 §4.1) — even with interception, the redirect never matched the server URL the browser was told to hit;
- a sheet resolution without a callback was treated as a user cancel → **silent paste-key fallback**, so the failure was invisible (owner ruling: no paste fallback, honest SSO only);
- `service.reconfigure` did not await the in-flight connect, letting the last-saved codemie row's reconfigure land after AIIN's (the 11:33:53 `baseUrl=codemie...` in the owner's log, F4);
- the CLI server's `close()` guard ran in `openFuture`'s microtask, so a same-microtask complete-then-close (cancel timeout, double tap) threw `Bad state: Cannot close sink while adding stream`.

- `aiin_connect_flow.dart`: pass `callbackScheme: 'http'`, bind on `localhost`, consume the callback URL returned by the channel and feed it to the CLI server's `onCallback` through a scoped `HttpOverrides` localhost alias, visible error on sheet-resolves-without-callback.
- `aiin_connect_server.dart`: single-flight latch, race-safe close, `/callback` + cancel-race logging (F1 vs F2 answerable from logs).
- `agent_service.dart` / `relay_agent_service.dart`: `reconfigure` awaits the in-flight connect (parity with #327).

- desktop-hop step tests made teardown-safe (real-async server binds inside `runAsync`).
- server tests: latch reuse, close-race, provider error callback surfacing, cancel/timeout.

64 flutter tests + 16 dart tests pass; no new analyzer issues.
EOF

# GitHub tracker comment

Use GitHub-flavored Markdown in `outputs/response.md` for GitHub issue
comments and descriptions. Your output is posted to the issue as-is — every
construct must render natively on GitHub.

- Headings: `##`, `###`
- Bullets: `- item`
- Numbered lists: `1. item`
- Bold: `**text**`
- Inline code: `` `code` ``
- Code block: ` ```lang ... ``` ` with a language tag (`dart`, `bash`, `json`)
- Link: `[text](url)`
- Tables: standard GFM table syntax (`|---|` separator row)

Do not use Jira wiki markup in GitHub fields: no `{code}...{code}` blocks,
no `{panel}` macros, no `h1.`/`h2.`/`h3.` heading prefixes, no
`{{monospace}}` inline code, no `[title|url]` links. None of it renders on
GitHub — a comment full of `{code}` fences and `h3.` headers is unreadable.

**IMPORTANT** When the issue references a parent story or related issues,
get them for full context using: `dmtools github_get_issue OWNER/REPO#NUMBER`
(the composite key form works directly).

# gh-1044: [BUG] iOS/MACos: AIIN (aiin.by) provider add — auth flow completes but provider never added; reconfigure binds to the CodeMie row

## Description

## Bug

On **iOS**, adding the **aiin.by** provider: the auth flow runs (loopback callback listener starts, browser sheet opens, sign-in completes on the page) — but **the AIIN provider never appears** in the providers list. Owner report (2026-09-28): «пытаюсь добавить aiin.by провайдер... прохожу auth flow но провайдер не добавляется. на ios». Owner rulings: AIIN «работает охрененно в браузере» (web reference behavior), and it must work exactly as well **on mobile and macOS** (app builds). Third ruling (2026-09-28, verbatim): «никаких фолбек на ключ... у нас там честный SSO должен быть... если что-то не получится то тогда надо будет мне в aiin.by адопшен запрашивать» — **no key-paste fallback at all; SSO is the only path**; if the SSO cannot be made to work client-side, the deliverable is a precise, evidence-backed adoption request for aiin.by (what to change on their side).

## Evidence (app log, iOS device, 2026-09-28)

```
11:33:03 [AIIN mobile] listening for the AIIN callback on http://127.0.0.1:65043/callback
11:33:32 [AIIN mobile] listening for the AIIN callback on http://127.0.0.1:65049/callback
11:33:35 [AIIN mobile] browser opened; sign in on the AIIN page
11:33:53 [Fa] reconfigure: baseUrl=https://codemie.lab.epam.com/code-assistant-api/v1,
           apiKey.len=190, isCodeMie=true, model.headers=[cookie]
11:33:58 [AIIN mobile] listening for the AIIN callback on http://127.0.0.1:65057/callback
```

Three listener starts (three Add taps), the browser sheet opened — and then **zero AIIN completion artifacts**: no model-picker push, no `[Fa] reconfigure` with `api.aiin.by`, no registry entry. The 11:33:53 reconfigure is **codemie** — see F4 below; it is NOT the AIIN flow (`_finishAiinConnect` always reconfigures with `aiinDefaultChatBaseUrl`).

## What the code does (read on origin/main; the local checkout predates this flow)

`flutter_app/lib/services/aiin_connect_flow.dart`:
- `runAiinConnectFlow` dispatches: web → `runAiinWebConnect` (the working popup path, #486); **mobile (iOS/Android) → `runAiinMobileConnect`** (#976); desktop → `_runAiinDesktopConnect`.
- `runAiinMobileConnect` runs the SAME loopback CLI server as desktop (`runAiinConnectCliFlow`, `lib/src/cli/aiin_connect_server.dart:152` logs the "listening" line) and opens the authorize URL in an **ASWebAuthenticationSession** sheet via the shared `fah/web_auth_session` MethodChannel (line ~311 — the same channel the CodeMie SSO flow drives).
- The design: the OAuth redirect (`http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback`) loads **inside the sheet**, hits the on-device server, `onCallback` dismisses the sheet, the server exchanges the code and returns `AiinConnectResult`.
- **`cancelWhenOpenSettles: authSession`** (iOS): the sheet resolving WITHOUT a server callback is treated as user cancel → `_completeAiinConnect` gets `result == null` → **silent paste-key fallback** (`_pasteAiinKeyFallback`). A user swipe and a lost race are indistinguishable by design.
- Success path: `_finishAiinConnect` → model picker from `api.aiin.by/v1/models` → registry entry named by account email → `service.reconfigure` (logs `baseUrl=api.aiin.by`).

## The CodeMie comparison (owner's pointer — decisive)

CodeMie SSO works on this exact iOS app through the SAME `fah/web_auth_session` channel. `AppDelegate.swift` (~lines 2284–2345) implements the native contract: `authenticate {url, callbackScheme}` creates the `ASWebAuthenticationSession`, **intercepts the redirect whose scheme matches `callbackScheme`** (iOS's RFC-8252 loopback interception), and **returns the callback URL to Dart**: `result(callbackURL?.absoluteString)` (or nil on user cancel).

CodeMie's Dart (`codemie_sso_flow.dart`, `systemAuthSessionCodeMieSso`) invokes it with **`callbackScheme: "http"`**, the redirect is `http://localhost:<port>/?token=...`, and the flow **consumes the returned URL** — extracting the token right out of it. WebView fallback only when the session cannot start.

AIIN's `_openAiinAuthSession` (aiin_connect_flow.dart ~319) breaks the contract in exactly two places:
1. **No `callbackScheme`** — it sends only `{'url': url}`; native reads `args["callbackScheme"]` → nil → **no interception**: the `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback` redirect becomes a plain in-sheet navigation, and the session's completion handler fires only on cancel.
2. **The return value is discarded** — `.then((_) => true)` throws the intercepted URL (when there is one) on the floor. CodeMie's flow builds its credentials from that URL; AIIN's Dart never looks at it.
The ticket confirms my root-cause understanding. Now let me check the acceptance criteria section of the ticket for the PR body checklist:

## Root cause

The iOS/macOS AIIN add-provider flow broke the shared `fah/web_auth_session` contract that CodeMie's working SSO flow honors, in two places (`_openAiinAuthSession`):

1. **No `callbackScheme` argument** — the native `ASWebAuthenticationSession` only intercepts the redirect when the requested scheme matches `callbackScheme`. 2. **The intercepted callback URL was discarded** (`.then((_) => true)`) — CodeMie's flow builds its credentials from that URL; AIIN's Dart never looked at it.

Compounding factors:

- the loopback listener bound on `127.0.0.1` while iOS auto-intercepts only the `localhost` host form (RFC 8252 §4.1) — even with interception, the redirect never matched the server URL the browser was told to hit;

# GitHub tracker comment

Use GitHub-flavored Markdown in `outputs/response.md` for GitHub issue
comments and descriptions. Your output is posted to the issue as-is — every
construct must render natively on GitHub.

- Headings: `##`, `###`
- Bullets: `- item`
- Numbered lists: `1. item`
- Bold: `**text**`
- Inline code: `` `code` ``
- Code block: ` ```lang ... ``` ` with a language tag (`dart`, `bash`, `json`)
- Link: `[text](url)`
- Tables: standard GFM table syntax (`|---|` separator row)

Do not use Jira wiki markup in GitHub fields: no `{code}...{code}` blocks,
no `{panel}` macros, no `h1.`/`h2.`/`h3.` heading prefixes, no
`{{monospace}}` inline code, no `[title|url]` links. None of it renders on
GitHub — a comment full of `{code}` fences and `h3.` headers is unreadable.

**IMPORTANT** When the issue references a parent story or related issues,
get them for full context using: `dmtools github_get_issue OWNER/REPO#NUMBER`
(the composite key form works directly).

mkdir -p outputs && cat > outputs/response.md <<'EOF'
## Fix shipped — [PR #1194](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1194)

**Root cause (F2 confirmed — no aiin.by-side change needed):** the iOS/macOS AIIN flow broke the shared `fah/web_auth_session` contract that CodeMie's working SSO flow honors:

1. `_openAiinAuthSession` sent no `callbackScheme` argument, so the native `ASWebAuthenticationSession` never intercepted the `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback` redirect — it became a plain in-sheet navigation and the session resolved only on cancel.
2. The intercepted callback URL was discarded (`.then((_) => true)`).
3. The loopback listener bound on `127.0.0.1` while iOS auto-intercepts only the `localhost` host form (RFC 8252 §4.1).

A sheet resolution without a callback was then treated as a silent paste-key fallback — the exact invisible failure in the owner's log (three listener starts, zero completion artifacts). `reconfigure` also did not await the in-flight connect, letting the codemie row's reconfigure land after AIIN's (the 11:33:53 `baseUrl=codemie...` line, F4).

**Fix:**

- pass `callbackScheme: 'http'`, bind on `localhost`, consume the callback URL returned by the channel and feed it to the CLI server's `onCallback` through a scoped `HttpOverrides` localhost alias;
- sheet-resolves-without-callback and cannot-start are now **visible errors** (no paste fallback — honest SSO per the owner ruling);
- CLI server: single-flight latch (retry reuses one live listener), race-safe close (was throwing `Bad state: Cannot close sink while adding stream` on the cancel timeout), `/callback` + cancel-race logging so F1 (proxy never redirects) stays answerable from logs;
- `reconfigure` awaits the in-flight connect (parity with #327) — no more codemie-row hijack.

**Acceptance criteria:**

| AC | Status |
|---|---|
| AC1 sign-in → provider row, model picker, `baseUrl=api.aiin.by` reconfigure | ✅ VM-tested success path |
| AC2 F1/F2 discrimination from logs | ✅ `/callback` hit, sheet resolution, race-outcome logs |
| AC3 one live listener per add attempt | ✅ single-flight latch + test |
| AC4 cancel/timeout/failure → visible error, no paste sheet | ✅ VM tests on `result == null` and sheet-settles-first |
| AC5 macOS desktop-loopback parity | ✅ same server code; desktop-hop step tests green |
| AC6 no codemie reconfigure during the AIIN flow | ✅ `reconfigure` in-flight guard + fakes assert the contract |
| AC7 VM tests: iOS override + mocked channel | ✅ callback-lands / cannot-start / sheet-settles / double-tap |
| AC8 adoption request | n/a — F2 was the root cause; F1 remains detectable from logs if it ever appears |
| AC9 CodeMie-parity wiring | ✅ `callbackScheme: 'http'`, `localhost` redirect host, URL consumed; VM-tested |

**Tests:** 64 flutter tests + 16 dart tests pass; no new analyzer issues.
EOF
gh issue comment 1044 --body-file outputs/response.md 2>&1 | tail -1

## Root cause

The iOS/macOS AIIN add-provider flow broke the shared `fah/web_auth_session` contract that CodeMie's working SSO flow honors, in two places (`_openAiinAuthSession`):

1. **No `callbackScheme` argument** — the native `ASWebAuthenticationSession` only intercepts the redirect when the requested scheme matches `callbackScheme`. AIIN sent only `{'url': ...}`, so the `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback` redirect became a plain in-sheet navigation and the session's completion handler fired only on user cancel.
2. **The intercepted callback URL was discarded** (`.then((_) => true)`) — CodeMie's flow builds its credentials from that URL; AIIN's Dart never looked at it.

Compounding factors:

- the loopback listener bound on `127.0.0.1` while iOS auto-intercepts only the `localhost` host form (RFC 8252 §4.1) — even with interception, the redirect never matched the server URL the browser was told to hit;
- a sheet resolution without a callback was treated as a user cancel → **silent paste-key fallback**, so the failure was invisible (owner ruling: no paste fallback, honest SSO only);
- `service.reconfigure` did not await the in-flight connect, letting the last-saved codemie row's reconfigure land after AIIN's (the 11:33:53 `baseUrl=codemie...` in the owner's log, F4);
- the CLI server's `close()` guard ran in `openFuture`'s microtask, so a same-microtask complete-then-close (cancel timeout, double tap) threw `Bad state: Cannot close sink while adding stream`.

## Fix

- `aiin_connect_flow.dart`: pass `callbackScheme: 'http'`, bind on `localhost`, consume the callback URL returned by the channel and feed it to the CLI server's `onCallback` through a scoped `HttpOverrides` localhost alias, visible error on sheet-resolves-without-callback.
- `aiin_connect_server.dart`: single-flight latch, race-safe close, `/callback` + cancel-race logging (F1 vs F2 answerable from logs).

- desktop-hop step tests made teardown-safe (real-async server binds inside `runAsync`).
- server tests: latch reuse, close-race, provider error callback surfacing, cancel/timeout.

64 flutter tests + 16 dart tests pass; no new analyzer issues.

## Root cause

The iOS/macOS AIIN add-provider flow broke the shared `fah/web_auth_session` contract that CodeMie's working SSO flow honors, in two places (`_openAiinAuthSession`):

1. **No `callbackScheme` argument** — the native `ASWebAuthenticationSession` only intercepts the redirect when the requested scheme matches `callbackScheme`. 2. **The intercepted callback URL was discarded** (`.then((_) => true)`) — CodeMie's flow builds its credentials from that URL; AIIN's Dart never looked at it.

- the loopback listener bound on `127.0.0.1` while iOS auto-intercepts only the `localhost` host form (RFC 8252 §4.1) — even with interception, the redirect never matched the server URL the browser was told to hit;

# gh-1044: [BUG] iOS/MACos: AIIN (aiin.by) provider add — auth flow completes but provider never added; reconfigure binds to the CodeMie row

## Description

## Bug

On **iOS**, adding the **aiin.by** provider: the auth flow runs (loopback callback listener starts, browser sheet opens, sign-in completes on the page) — but **the AIIN provider never appears** in the providers list. Owner report (2026-09-28): «пытаюсь добавить aiin.by провайдер... прохожу auth flow но провайдер не добавляется. на ios». Owner rulings: AIIN «работает охрененно в браузере» (web reference behavior), and it must work exactly as well **on mobile and macOS** (app builds). Third ruling (2026-09-28, verbatim): «никаких фолбек на ключ... у нас там честный SSO должен быть... если что-то не получится то тогда надо будет мне в aiin.by адопшен запрашивать» — **no key-paste fallback at all; SSO is the only path**; if the SSO cannot be made to work client-side, the deliverable is a precise, evidence-backed adoption request for aiin.by (what to change on their side).

## Evidence (app log, iOS device, 2026-09-28)

```
11:33:03 [AIIN mobile] listening for the AIIN callback on http://127.0.0.1:65043/callback
11:33:32 [AIIN mobile] listening for the AIIN callback on http://127.0.0.1:65049/callback
11:33:35 [AIIN mobile] browser opened; sign in on the AIIN page
11:33:53 [Fa] reconfigure: baseUrl=https://codemie.lab.epam.com/code-assistant-api/v1,
           apiKey.len=190, isCodeMie=true, model.headers=[cookie]
11:33:58 [AIIN mobile] listening for the AIIN callback on http://127.0.0.1:65057/callback
```

Three listener starts (three Add taps), the browser sheet opened — and then **zero AIIN completion artifacts**: no model-picker push, no `[Fa] reconfigure` with `api.aiin.by`, no registry entry. The 11:33:53 reconfigure is **codemie** — see F4 below; it is NOT the AIIN flow (`_finishAiinConnect` always reconfigures with `aiinDefaultChatBaseUrl`).

## What the code does (read on origin/main; the local checkout predates this flow)

`flutter_app/lib/services/aiin_connect_flow.dart`:
- `runAiinConnectFlow` dispatches: web → `runAiinWebConnect` (the working popup path, #486); **mobile (iOS/Android) → `runAiinMobileConnect`** (#976); desktop → `_runAiinDesktopConnect`.
- `runAiinMobileConnect` runs the SAME loopback CLI server as desktop (`runAiinConnectCliFlow`, `lib/src/cli/aiin_connect_server.dart:152` logs the "listening" line) and opens the authorize URL in an **ASWebAuthenticationSession** sheet via the shared `fah/web_auth_session` MethodChannel (line ~311 — the same channel the CodeMie SSO flow drives).
- The design: the OAuth redirect (`http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback`) loads **inside the sheet**, hits the on-device server, `onCallback` dismisses the sheet, the server exchanges the code and returns `AiinConnectResult`.
- **`cancelWhenOpenSettles: authSession`** (iOS): the sheet resolving WITHOUT a server callback is treated as user cancel → `_completeAiinConnect` gets `result == null` → **silent paste-key fallback** (`_pasteAiinKeyFallback`). A user swipe and a lost race are indistinguishable by design.
- Success path: `_finishAiinConnect` → model picker from `api.aiin.by/v1/models` → registry entry named by account email → `service.reconfigure` (logs `baseUrl=api.aiin.by`).

## The CodeMie comparison (owner's pointer — decisive)

CodeMie SSO works on this exact iOS app through the SAME `fah/web_auth_session` channel. `AppDelegate.swift` (~lines 2284–2345) implements the native contract: `authenticate {url, callbackScheme}` creates the `ASWebAuthenticationSession`, **intercepts the redirect whose scheme matches `callbackScheme`** (iOS's RFC-8252 loopback interception), and **returns the callback URL to Dart**: `result(callbackURL?.absoluteString)` (or nil on user cancel).

CodeMie's Dart (`codemie_sso_flow.dart`, `systemAuthSessionCodeMieSso`) invokes it with **`callbackScheme: "http"`**, the redirect is `http://localhost:<port>/?token=...`, and the flow **consumes the returned URL** — extracting the token right out of it. WebView fallback only when the session cannot start.

AIIN's `_openAiinAuthSession` (aiin_connect_flow.dart ~319) breaks the contract in exactly two places:
1. **No `callbackScheme`** — it sends only `{'url': url}`; native reads `args["callbackScheme"]` → nil → **no interception**: the `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback` redirect becomes a plain in-sheet navigation, and the session's completion handler fires only on cancel.
2. **The return value is discarded** — `.then((_) => true)` throws the intercepted URL (when there is one) on the floor. CodeMie's flow builds its credentials from that URL; AIIN's Dart never looks at it.

## Root cause

The iOS/macOS AIIN add-provider flow broke the shared `fah/web_auth_session` contract that CodeMie's working SSO flow honors, in two places (`_openAiinAuthSession`):

1. **No `callbackScheme` argument** — the native `ASWebAuthenticationSession` only intercepts the redirect when the requested scheme matches `callbackScheme`. AIIN sent only `{'url': ...}`, so the `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback` redirect became a plain in-sheet navigation and the session's completion handler fired only on user cancel.
2. **The intercepted callback URL was discarded** (`.then((_) => true)`) — CodeMie's flow builds its credentials from that URL; AIIN's Dart never looked at it.

Compounding factors:

- the loopback listener bound on `127.0.0.1` while iOS auto-intercepts only the `localhost` host form (RFC 8252 §4.1) — even with interception, the redirect never matched the server URL the browser was told to hit;
- a sheet resolution without a callback was treated as a user cancel → **silent paste-key fallback**, so the failure was invisible (owner ruling: no paste fallback, honest SSO only);
- `service.reconfigure` did not await the in-flight connect, letting the last-saved codemie row's reconfigure land after AIIN's (the 11:33:53 `baseUrl=codemie...` in the owner's log, F4);
